intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Polygon. Native AVAX is what leaves C-Chain, and Polygon WETH is what can arrive: an ERC-20 claim on ether, not POL, and not ETH sitting on Ethereum.

The source side is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the native gas sentinel, on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace is the explorer for that send. The WETH you want on Polygon is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Confirm it on Polygonscan. Polygon is chain id 137, and gas there is POL, so WETH cannot pay the next transaction.
description: AVAX leaves Avalanche C-Chain and WETH arrives on Polygon. Pay AVAX, then hold POL for gas. Match both contracts on Snowtrace and Polygonscan before you sign.

sections.heading: C-Chain AVAX is the only balance this quote spends
sections.body: Avalanche C-Chain charges the outbound fee in AVAX. The sentinel address is native gas, not an ERC-20 you approve. An X-Chain or P-Chain balance will not fund this quote, even if the wallet labels it AVAX. If the network badge is not chain id 43114, stop and switch before you type an amount. Selling the entire AVAX balance also fails, because the fee is AVAX too.

sections.heading: Polygon WETH cannot cover the POL fee
sections.body: Polygon WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 is a wrapped ether ERC-20. It is not native ETH, and it is not the WETH contract on Ethereum. ETH and WETH are different instruments. WBTC is a different wrapped claim and is not native bitcoin; this route does not deliver it. After the WETH balance shows on Polygonscan, you still need POL on chain id 137 to move it.

sections.heading: Skip this hop when POL or mainnet ether is the goal
sections.body: This route is the wrong job if you need POL for gas, Circle USDC, or Tether USDT. It is also wrong if you wanted ether on Ethereum, chain id 1, where blocks are about 12 seconds and the explorer is Etherscan. Stay on C-Chain when the pool you want already quotes AVAX there. Bridging out only to swap and come back pays fees twice. The minimum on the quote is the floor, and there is no clock on the bridge.

sections.heading: Pair Snowtrace with Polygonscan before the signature
sections.body: Match the source sentinel on Snowtrace and the WETH contract on Polygonscan before you sign in your own wallet. The lock, proof, and release steps are the subject of [how cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work). Start with a size you can afford to see fail. If the wallet still says MATIC, confirm the network is Polygon and the gas asset is POL.

faqs.question: Does AVAX to Polygon WETH deliver ETH on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. AVAX leaves Avalanche C-Chain and WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 is what can arrive on Polygon. Native ETH on Ethereum is chain id 1 and pays gas there. WETH is an ERC-20, so it cannot pay POL gas on Polygon either. Check Polygonscan for the arrival, not Etherscan.

faqs.question: What does the 0xEeee address mean on the AVAX side?
faqs.answer: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is the native gas sentinel for AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. It is not an ERC-20 you approve, and it is not an X-Chain balance. Snowtrace is where you confirm the send. Keep some AVAX so the source transaction can pay its own fee.

faqs.question: Should I use this route if I only need POL?
faqs.answer: No. This page is wrong when you want POL, the Polygon gas token on chain id 137. WETH is a wrapped ether contract, not the fee coin. If you already hold a Polygon asset that trades against WETH, swap on Polygon and skip the bridge. The quote minimum is the floor.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to POL on Polygon. AVAX leaves C-Chain as the gas coin you spend, and native POL is what can arrive on Polygon to pay fees there.

Both legs of this quote use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. That string is the native gas sentinel, not one shared token. On the way out it means AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, which you check on Snowtrace. On the way in it means POL on Polygon, chain id 137, which you check on Polygonscan. The same letters do not make the balances interchangeable.
description: AVAX leaves Avalanche C-Chain and POL arrives on Polygon. Both are gas tokens. Confirm chain ids 43114 and 137 on Snowtrace and Polygonscan before you sign.

sections.heading: One sentinel string, two native coins
sections.body: Wallets reuse 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE whenever the asset is the chain's own gas. AVAX on C-Chain and POL on Polygon both qualify, and neither is an ERC-20 approval. You do not get a contract address to paste into a token import for the received POL. You get a native balance on chain id 137. If a form asks you to approve POL like USDC, you are on the wrong screen.

sections.heading: X-Chain AVAX never enters this quote
sections.body: Avalanche has more than one chain. This route spends C-Chain AVAX only. An X-Chain or P-Chain address will not sign the EVM transaction, and Snowtrace will not show an X-Chain transfer as this send. Chain id 43114 has to be the network in the wallet before the amount matters. Leave a little AVAX behind so the outbound fee can clear.

sections.heading: POL is the fee coin, not a stand-in for WETH
sections.body: People still say MATIC out of habit. The gas asset on Polygon is POL. It is not WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619, and it is not Circle USDC or Tether USDT. ETH on Ethereum is a third coin again, on chain id 1, with about 12 second blocks and Etherscan as the explorer. If your next trade needs wrapped ether, this arrival cannot fill that contract.

sections.heading: When a same-chain swap already solves it
sections.body: Use this route when Polygon is where you need gas and the AVAX is what you can spare. Skip it when both legs of the trade already exist on C-Chain, or when you only wanted to rebalance AVAX inside Avalanche. A bridge is the wrong tool for a local pool. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the network note for the arrival side. Read the minimum received and refuse the quote if that floor is too low.

sections.heading: What to compare on the two explorers
sections.body: Snowtrace should show native AVAX leaving a C-Chain address. Polygonscan should later show native POL on the destination address, on chain id 137. There is no ERC-20 transfer log for the gas itself. Do not treat a missing token-transfer row as a failed delivery until you have checked the native balance. The bridge wait sits on top of both chains, and this page does not time it.

faqs.question: Why do both sides of AVAX to POL show the same address?
faqs.answer: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE marks native gas, not a shared contract. On Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, it is AVAX. On Polygon, chain id 137, it is POL. Snowtrace and Polygonscan are different explorers. Importing that address as an ERC-20 will not show the balance you are about to receive.

faqs.question: Can I send X-Chain AVAX on this route?
faqs.answer: No. This quote spends C-Chain AVAX only. X-Chain and P-Chain balances do not sign this EVM transaction. Switch the wallet to chain id 43114 and confirm the account on Snowtrace. Keep enough AVAX to pay the outbound fee, or the send cannot be broadcast. Polygonscan is where native POL should show up later.

faqs.question: Is this the right route if I need WETH on Polygon?
faqs.answer: No. POL is the gas token that arrives, and WETH is a separate ERC-20. If a pool or a contract asks for wrapped ether, this page is the wrong arrival. You would still need POL afterward to move that WETH. Stay with a WETH route instead of hoping POL will be accepted as ether.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to USDT on Arbitrum One. Circle USDC leaves C-Chain, and Tether USDT is what can arrive on Arbitrum One. The dollar ticker changes with the chain.

You send 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, Circle's native USDC on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace is the explorer. The arrival contract is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, Tether's USDT on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Arbitrum Nova. Arbiscan is where that contract has to match. Gas out is AVAX. Gas in is ETH, and the USDT you receive will not pay it.
description: Circle USDC leaves Avalanche C-Chain and Tether USDT arrives on Arbitrum One. Pay AVAX, then hold ETH. Check Snowtrace and Arbiscan before you sign it.

sections.heading: Circle and Tether are not a rename
sections.body: USDC here is Circle. USDT there is Tether. A desk, a payroll file, or a lending market that names one issuer will reject the other even when the price looks like a dollar. This route is the wrong page if the Arbitrum balance you need is Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. It is also wrong if you still hold bridged USDC.e and expect this native Circle contract on C-Chain to spend it.

sections.heading: Arbitrum One is chain id 42161
sections.body: Nova is a different network. A wallet parked on Nova, or still on C-Chain, will not show the USDT this quote delivers. Arbiscan, not Snowtrace, is the arrival explorer. Blocks on the two chains do not set the bridge wait. AVAX on chain id 43114 pays the source fee. After USDT lands you still need ETH on Arbitrum One, because a stablecoin is not the gas token.

sections.heading: Approval stays on the Avalanche USDC contract
sections.body: Circle's C-Chain USDC is an ERC-20, so the wallet can ask for an approval before the bridge. That approval is for 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E only. It does not authorize Tether, and it does not move funds by itself. If the spender is not the contract the quote names, reject it. The steps from a signed source transfer to a destination balance are laid out in [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains).

sections.heading: Stay on one issuer when the chain is the only change you need
sections.body: If you already need USDC on Arbitrum, switching into Tether adds an issuer you did not ask for. If you already need USDT on C-Chain, you may not need to leave Avalanche at all. Compare the minimum received with the dollar amount you are trying to keep. A thin route can shave the stablecoin even when both tickers are supposed to track a dollar. Do not sign a floor you would not accept.

faqs.question: Will this Avalanche USDC arrive as USDC on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: No. Circle USDC leaves Avalanche C-Chain and Tether USDT at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 is what can arrive on Arbitrum One. Circle's own USDC on that network is a different contract. Confirm the arrival on Arbiscan. If your receiver only accepts Circle, this route is the wrong one.

faqs.question: Does USDT on Arbitrum pay the gas?
faqs.answer: No. Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, charges gas in ETH, not in USDT and not in AVAX. The source fee is AVAX on C-Chain, chain id 43114. Keep ETH on Arbitrum before you try to move the USDT that lands. Nova is a different network and will not show this balance.

faqs.question: Which USDC contract does this route spend?
faqs.answer: It spends Circle's native USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Avalanche C-Chain. Snowtrace is the check. Bridged USDC.e is a different contract, and an X-Chain balance is not this token at all. If the wallet holds the wrong USDC, the quote cannot spend it. Keep AVAX for the fee on chain id 43114.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on Arbitrum One. Circle USDC leaves C-Chain, and native ETH is what can arrive on Arbitrum One, ready to pay gas there.

The USDC you spend is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Check that contract on Snowtrace before you approve it. The ETH you receive is quoted as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the native gas sentinel, on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Arbiscan shows the arrival as ETH, not as an ERC-20 transfer. This is not WETH, and it is not ETH on Ethereum mainnet.
description: Circle USDC leaves Avalanche C-Chain and native ETH arrives on Arbitrum One. Pay AVAX, then use ETH for gas. Check Snowtrace and Arbiscan before you sign.

sections.heading: You are buying the L2 fee token
sections.body: Arbitrum One takes ETH for gas. AVAX from C-Chain will not show up as a spendable fee balance after you change networks. This route exists so a Circle dollar balance on Avalanche can become that ETH. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means native gas on the destination. You do not approve it the way you approve USDC. If the wallet asks you to import that address as a token, close that screen and look at the native ETH line instead.

sections.heading: Mainnet ether is a different account of the same ticker
sections.body: Ethereum is chain id 1. Blocks there are about 12 seconds, and the explorer is Etherscan. Arbitrum One is chain id 42161, and Arbiscan is the explorer. ETH on one does not pay a transaction on the other. Nova is not this route either. If someone sent you a mainnet address and told you the gas was covered, this arrival still sits on Arbitrum until you bridge again.

sections.heading: Use the WETH route when the pool rejects native ETH
sections.body: Some contracts accept only wrapped ether. WETH on Arbitrum One is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, an ERC-20. Native ETH cannot satisfy that call until it is wrapped. WBTC is not a substitute either, and WBTC is not native bitcoin. If the app you are funding wants WETH inventory, this page is the wrong arrival even though both tickers refer to ether. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) keeps the gas and network notes in one place.

sections.heading: Leave AVAX on C-Chain for the exit
sections.body: The source fee is still AVAX, chain id 43114. An empty AVAX balance stops the USDC transfer before Arbitrum ever sees it. Circle's token can require an approval; limit that approval to the amount you are moving when the wallet lets you. Read the minimum ETH on the quote. Dollar-to-ETH prices move, and a stale floor is a reason to request a new quote rather than sign.

faqs.question: Is the ETH from this route WETH on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: No. Circle USDC leaves Avalanche and native ETH arrives, quoted as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Arbitrum One. WETH is the separate contract 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Native ETH pays gas. WETH does not. If the next app wants the wrapper, switch routes before you sign. Arbiscan is the explorer on chain id 42161.

faqs.question: Can this ETH pay fees on Ethereum mainnet?
faqs.answer: No. The arrival is Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, which you check on Arbiscan. Ethereum mainnet is chain id 1, with about 12 second blocks and Etherscan. The two ETH balances do not mix. Nova is a third network. AVAX on C-Chain paid the source fee and does not travel as gas.

faqs.question: What USDC does the Avalanche side spend?
faqs.answer: Circle's native USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, chain id 43114. Snowtrace is the explorer. Bridged USDC.e will not match this quote. You may be asked to approve that Circle contract. Keep a little AVAX so the approval and the send can both pay their fees. X-Chain AVAX is not this balance.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Arbitrum One. Circle USDC leaves C-Chain, and Arbitrum WETH is what can arrive: wrapped ether for contracts, not the ETH that pays gas.

Spend 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, Circle's USDC on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, and confirm it on Snowtrace. The WETH contract is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, which you confirm on Arbiscan. That address is not the native sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, not Ethereum WETH, and not Base WETH. Nova will not show this balance.
description: Circle USDC leaves Avalanche C-Chain and WETH arrives on Arbitrum One. WETH is not gas. Pay AVAX, then hold ETH. Check Snowtrace and Arbiscan before you sign.

sections.heading: The wrapper is inventory, not the fee
sections.body: WETH exists so protocols can move ether under ERC-20 rules. It does not pay Arbitrum gas. After this route, a wallet can hold WETH and still fail the next transaction for lack of ETH. If the only thing you need is fee balance, the native ETH route is the one that matches the job. Signing this page and then wrapping nothing you can spend is a wasted hop.

sections.heading: Match 0x82aF on Arbiscan, not a lookalike WETH
sections.body: Ethereum's canonical WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1. Polygon and Base use different WETH addresses again. Pasting the wrong one into a token list shows a zero balance and invites a fake. WBTC is another wrapper and is not native bitcoin; this quote does not deliver it. Arbiscan is the only explorer that proves 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on chain id 42161.

sections.heading: Circle on C-Chain has to be the native contract
sections.body: The source token is Circle, not Tether, and not bridged USDC.e. An approval, if the wallet raises one, should name 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E and a spender you recognize from the quote. AVAX still pays that approval on chain id 43114. Snowtrace is where you watch the USDC leave. The bridge's own wait is separate from C-Chain confirmation, and nothing here clocks it.

sections.heading: Wrong page for a gas top-up or a mainnet pool
sections.body: Choose another route if the destination contract wants native ETH, if you needed Tether USDT, or if the pool you care about sits on Ethereum. A round trip off C-Chain and back only makes sense when Arbitrum WETH is the inventory you intend to hold. How a lock on one chain becomes a release on another is covered in [how cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work). Refuse the quote when the minimum WETH is below what you will accept.

faqs.question: Can Arbitrum WETH from this swap pay gas?
faqs.answer: No. WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is an ERC-20. Gas on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, is native ETH. Circle USDC left Avalanche C-Chain and became the wrapper, not the fee coin. Hold ETH before you try to spend the WETH. Check the arrival on Arbiscan. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Is this the same WETH as on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1, and Etherscan is that explorer. This route delivers Arbitrum WETH only. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds and do not describe this bridge. Nova is not Arbitrum One. Confirm chain id 42161 in the wallet.

faqs.question: What if I hold USDC.e instead of native USDC?
faqs.answer: Then this quote is pointed at the wrong balance. It spends Circle USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace will show a different contract for bridged USDC.e. Swap or bridge into the native Circle token first, and keep AVAX for the fee. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to ARB on Arbitrum One. Circle USDC leaves C-Chain, and the ARB token is what can arrive. You are leaving a dollar claim for a governance asset.

The USDC contract is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace should list that Circle token, not a bridged lookalike. ARB arrives at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Arbiscan is the check. ARB does not pay gas. ETH does. If you needed a stablecoin or a fee top-up, this route is the wrong shape.
description: Circle USDC leaves Avalanche C-Chain and ARB arrives on Arbitrum One. ARB is not gas. Pay AVAX, then hold ETH. Check Snowtrace and Arbiscan before you sign.

sections.heading: ARB is the governance token, not a dollar
sections.body: Circle USDC is built to track a dollar. ARB trades as the Arbitrum governance token and can move sharply while the bridge is still unfinished. The minimum received is your protection, and a quote that converts too little USDC into too little ARB should be rejected. This page is wrong when the treasury rule is to stay in Circle or Tether. It is also wrong when the only gap on Arbitrum is ETH for fees.

sections.heading: You still need ETH after ARB shows up
sections.body: Chain id 42161 charges ETH. A full ARB balance with an empty ETH line cannot approve, transfer, or vote. The source side is the opposite problem: AVAX on chain id 43114 has to remain above zero or the USDC never leaves. Native gas uses the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on each chain, and neither sentinel is the ARB contract. Do not paste ARB's address into the gas field.

sections.heading: Nova, mainnet, and C-Chain will not display this ARB
sections.body: Arbitrum Nova is not Arbitrum One. Ethereum mainnet, chain id 1, uses Etherscan and about 12 second blocks, and it does not hold this ARB balance. Snowtrace proves the USDC exit. Arbiscan proves the ARB entry. If the receiving wallet is still set to Avalanche, the arrival can look missing when it is only on the wrong network. Switch to chain id 42161 before you call the route a failure.

sections.heading: A local dollar swap is enough when you are not buying ARB
sections.body: If the goal is Tether, or USDC that already lives on Arbitrum, pick that pair instead of taking governance risk. If the goal is to keep dollars on C-Chain, do not bridge. [Avalanche C-Chain](/chains/avalanche) is the note for the network you are leaving. Size the first transfer so a bad minimum hurts less than the full amount, and do not treat a block time as a delivery promise.

faqs.question: Does ARB from this route pay Arbitrum gas?
faqs.answer: No. ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is the governance token. Gas on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, is ETH. Circle USDC left Avalanche C-Chain and did not become that ETH. Keep an ETH balance before you move ARB. Confirm the token on Arbiscan, and do not confuse this network with Nova.

faqs.question: Why is this a poor fit for a dollar treasury?
faqs.answer: Because the arrival is ARB, not Circle USDC and not Tether USDT. The price can move away from the dollar you spent at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. If the rule is to hold a stablecoin, this route is wrong. Read the minimum ARB and refuse a floor you would not keep.

faqs.question: Which explorer shows the USDC leaving C-Chain?
faqs.answer: Snowtrace, on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. The contract is Circle's native USDC, not bridged USDC.e, and not an X-Chain balance. AVAX pays the fee, so do not spend the last AVAX. Arbiscan is only for the ARB that can arrive later, on chain id 42161.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on Arbitrum One. Tether USDT leaves C-Chain, and Circle USDC is what can arrive on Arbitrum One. You change issuer and network together.

The Tether contract you spend is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace is the source explorer. Circle's native USDC on Arbitrum One is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, chain id 42161, and Arbiscan is where it has to match. Bridged USDC.e is a different token. AVAX pays the outbound fee. ETH pays every fee after USDC lands.
description: Tether USDT leaves Avalanche C-Chain and Circle USDC arrives on Arbitrum One. Pay AVAX, then hold ETH. Check Snowtrace and Arbiscan before you sign it.

sections.heading: Native USDC is not the bridged USDC.e balance
sections.body: Older Arbitrum apps still point at bridged USDC.e. This route does not deliver that contract. It delivers Circle's native USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. If a pool, a bridge refund, or a payroll file names USDC.e, stop. You would be holding the right ticker on the right chain id and still fail the transfer. The fix is a different destination, not a second signature on this quote.

sections.heading: Tether on C-Chain has its own address
sections.body: Do not approve Circle's Avalanche USDC and expect this quote to spend it. The source is Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Snowtrace should show that contract losing balance. Chain id 43114 has to be selected, because an X-Chain USDT idea is not a thing this wallet can sign. Keep AVAX for the fee. An approval of the wrong spender is a reason to reject the wallet screen.

sections.heading: ETH on Arbitrum One is a separate chore
sections.body: USDC cannot pay gas on chain id 42161. ETH can. Nova cannot. Ethereum mainnet, chain id 1, with about 12 second blocks and Etherscan, is a third place your new USDC will not appear. The native gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is how quotes mark ETH or AVAX, and it is not the USDC contract. Fund a little ETH before you try to use the dollars.

sections.heading: Keep Tether if the receiver is Tether
sections.body: Arbitrum already has Tether USDT at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. If that is the contract your counterparty named, this Circle arrival is the wrong route. Switching issuers can be right when the deep pool is USDC, and wrong when the invoice says USDT. The click path is [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains). Take the minimum received as the floor.

faqs.question: Does this route deliver bridged USDC.e on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: No. Tether USDT leaves Avalanche and Circle's native USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 is what can arrive on Arbitrum One. USDC.e is a different contract. Check Arbiscan on chain id 42161. If the app still wants the bridged token, this page is the wrong arrival. Snowtrace is only the source explorer.

faqs.question: Which contract is the Avalanche USDT?
faqs.answer: Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace is the explorer. It is not Circle USDC, and it is not an X-Chain balance. AVAX pays the source fee. Approve only that Tether contract, and only a spender that matches the quote you are reading.

faqs.question: Will the USDC I receive pay Arbitrum fees?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on Arbitrum One is ETH, not USDC and not AVAX. Chain id 42161 is the network, and Nova will not show this USDC. Hold ETH before you move the dollars. The bridge does not publish a delivery clock, so judge the quote by its minimum, not by a hoped-for wait.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on Arbitrum One. Tether USDT leaves C-Chain, and native ETH is what can arrive on Arbitrum One to pay gas.

You spend Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace records that send. The destination is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the native gas sentinel, which on Arbitrum One means ETH, chain id 42161. Arbiscan shows a native balance, not an ERC-20 log for the gas itself. This is not WETH, not AVAX, and not ether on Ethereum.
description: Tether USDT leaves Avalanche C-Chain and native ETH arrives on Arbitrum One. Pay AVAX, then use ETH for gas. Check Snowtrace and Arbiscan before you sign.

sections.heading: The sentinel on Arbitrum means ETH
sections.body: Quotes reuse 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE for whatever coin pays gas on that chain. Here the arrival is ETH on Arbitrum One. You do not approve that address. You receive a native balance you can spend on fees. If a token list invites you to add the sentinel as an ERC-20, ignore it and read the ETH row. WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is the wrapper route, and this page will not fill a contract that accepts only WETH.

sections.heading: Tether is the source, Circle is not
sections.body: A Circle USDC balance on C-Chain will sit untouched while this quote looks for 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. That is Tether. Confirm the holder and the amount on Snowtrace. Chain id 43114 only: X-Chain addresses do not sign this. AVAX pays the fee, so a wallet that converts every AVAX into the bridge input will fail before Arbitrum is involved.

sections.heading: Do not budget this ETH as mainnet gas
sections.body: Ethereum, chain id 1, finalizes blocks in about 12 seconds and uses Etherscan. Arbitrum One is chain id 42161 and uses Arbiscan. Nova is neither. ETH you receive here cannot cover a mainnet approval. It also cannot cover a C-Chain transaction, which still wants AVAX. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) spells out that split. The bridge adds its own wait on top of both networks, and this page does not promise when the ETH row updates.

sections.heading: A stable-to-stable route is calmer when you do not need gas
sections.body: Buying ETH means taking ether's price for the minutes the quote is open. If the Arbitrum balance you lack is USDC or USDT, stay in dollars. If you need WETH for a pool, use the wrapper route so you are not stuck unwrapping later. Compare the minimum ETH with the dollar value you are spending. Sign only if that floor is still worth the gas you are trying to buy.

faqs.question: Is the arrival WETH or native ETH?
faqs.answer: Native ETH. The quote uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the gas sentinel, on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. WETH is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 and is a different route. Tether USDT left Avalanche C-Chain. Check Arbiscan for the ETH balance, not an ERC-20 transfer of the sentinel. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

faqs.question: Can I spend Circle USDC on this quote?
faqs.answer: No. The source is Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace should show that contract. Circle USDC is a separate Avalanche token. X-Chain funds do not apply. Keep AVAX for the network fee or the send cannot be broadcast. Snowtrace is the check before you approve.

faqs.question: Will this ETH work on Ethereum or on Nova?
faqs.answer: No. It arrives on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Ethereum is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan. Nova is a different Arbitrum network. None of those balances pay each other's fees. Use the ETH on chain id 42161, and read the quote minimum before you sign.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Arbitrum One. Tether USDT leaves C-Chain, and Arbitrum WETH is what can arrive. The wrapper is inventory, not the coin that pays fees.

Spend 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, Tether on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, and watch it on Snowtrace. Receive 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, and match it on Arbiscan. That contract is not native ETH, so the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is the wrong mental model for the arrival. It is also not Ethereum's WETH and not WBTC, which is not native bitcoin.
description: Tether USDT leaves Avalanche C-Chain and WETH arrives on Arbitrum One. WETH is not gas. Pay AVAX, then hold ETH. Check Snowtrace and Arbiscan before you sign.

sections.heading: Hold ETH beside the WETH or the next click fails
sections.body: A wallet can show a healthy WETH balance and still be unable to transfer it. Arbitrum One bills ETH for gas. This route does not deliver that ETH. If your shortfall is fees, use the native ETH route instead of this one. If your shortfall is an ERC-20 the pool will accept, WETH is the arrival that matches. Mixing those jobs is how people bridge twice.

sections.heading: Only this Tether contract funds the quote
sections.body: Circle USDC on C-Chain is a different issuer and a different address. Bridged lookalikes will not satisfy 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Snowtrace is the proof that Tether left. Chain id 43114 must be selected. X-Chain balances do not sign EVM calls. Leave AVAX in the account so the approval, if one is required, and the send can both pay.

sections.heading: Arbiscan has to show 0x82aF, not a pasted mainnet address
sections.body: Ethereum WETH lives at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1, where blocks take about 12 seconds and Etherscan is the explorer. Importing that address on Arbitrum shows the wrong token or an empty balance. Nova is a different network again. The arrival you are checking is chain id 42161 only. A block interval on either chain is not a delivery time for the bridge.

sections.heading: Leave this page when the goal is gas or a stablecoin
sections.body: Tether into WETH takes price risk that a USDT-to-USDC hop does not. Skip this route if the receiver wants dollars, or if you are only topping up ETH. The lock and release pattern is explained in [how cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work). Read the minimum WETH. If that floor is worse than the ether exposure you want, do not sign.

faqs.question: Does this WETH pay gas on Arbitrum One?
faqs.answer: No. WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is an ERC-20, and gas is native ETH on chain id 42161. Tether USDT left Avalanche C-Chain and became the wrapper, not the fee coin. Hold ETH before you move the WETH. Confirm the contract on Arbiscan, not on Snowtrace. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

faqs.question: Is the source Circle USDC or Tether USDT?
faqs.answer: Tether, at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Circle's USDC will not be spent by this quote. Snowtrace is the explorer. Keep AVAX for the fee, and ignore X-Chain balances. An approval should name this Tether contract only. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

faqs.question: What if the pool I need is on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Then this route is wrong. It delivers Arbitrum WETH, not the canonical WETH on chain id 1. Etherscan and a 12 second block time belong to mainnet. Nova will not show this balance either. Stay on the chain where the pool already has depth, instead of bridging into a wrapper you must move again.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to ARB on Arbitrum One. Tether USDT leaves C-Chain, and the ARB governance token is what can arrive. A dollar claim becomes a volatile asset.

The USDT you send is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace should show Tether, not Circle. ARB is 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Arbiscan is the arrival explorer. ARB is not gas. ETH is. If the point of the transfer was to keep dollars or to buy fees, you are on the wrong route.
description: Tether USDT leaves Avalanche C-Chain and ARB arrives on Arbitrum One. ARB is not the fee token. Pay AVAX, then hold ETH. Check Snowtrace and Arbiscan.

sections.heading: You are exiting a stablecoin into governance exposure
sections.body: Tether is built to hold near a dollar. ARB is not. The quote's minimum is the only number that limits how much governance token you accept for the USDT you give up. A route that looks fine at one price can be a poor trade a moment later. This page is the wrong choice for a treasury that must remain in Tether or Circle, and it is the wrong choice if the missing piece is ETH for gas.

sections.heading: ARB cannot pay the transaction that moves ARB
sections.body: Chain id 42161 charges ETH. The native sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE marks that gas, not the ARB contract. Arrive with ARB and an empty ETH balance and you still cannot transfer, vote, or sell. On the way out, AVAX on chain id 43114 plays the same role. Spend the last AVAX and the USDT never leaves Snowtrace.

sections.heading: Three networks people confuse with this ARB
sections.body: Arbitrum Nova will not list this token. Ethereum mainnet, chain id 1, uses Etherscan and about 12 second blocks, and it is not the destination. C-Chain is only the source. If the wallet network is still 43114 after you sign, the ARB can be confirmed on Arbiscan while the wallet shows zero. Switch to 42161 before you resend. Resending is how the same USDT gets spent twice.

sections.heading: Pick a dollar route when ARB was not the request
sections.body: USDT to USDC stays inside stablecoins. USDT to ETH buys the fee token. USDT to WETH buys the wrapper. This page is only for someone who wants 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. The practical sequence is in [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains). Judge the floor on the quote, and do not treat either chain's block time as an arrival promise.

faqs.question: Will the ARB I receive cover Arbitrum fees?
faqs.answer: No. ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 does not pay gas. ETH does, on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Tether USDT left Avalanche C-Chain and became the governance token, not the fee coin. Keep ETH in the destination wallet. Check Arbiscan, and do not look for this balance on Nova.

faqs.question: Is this a good route for keeping dollars?
faqs.answer: No. The arrival is ARB, which can move away from the dollar you spent as Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. If the receiver wants USDT or Circle USDC, choose that route. Snowtrace confirms the source on chain id 43114. The minimum ARB on the quote is the floor you either accept or reject.

faqs.question: What pays the fee on the Avalanche side?
faqs.answer: AVAX, on C-Chain, chain id 43114. The sentinel for that native gas is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and it is not the USDT contract. X-Chain AVAX will not sign this. Snowtrace is the explorer for the Tether leaving. Leave enough AVAX that the send can still be broadcast.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on Arbitrum One. Native AVAX leaves C-Chain, and Circle USDC is what can arrive on Arbitrum One.

The AVAX you spend is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the native gas sentinel, on chain id 43114. Snowtrace shows that as AVAX, not as an ERC-20. Circle's USDC on Arbitrum One is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, chain id 42161, and Arbiscan is the check. This is not bridged USDC.e, not Tether, and not ETH. You are selling the C-Chain fee coin, so the amount has to leave some AVAX behind.
description: AVAX leaves Avalanche C-Chain and Circle USDC arrives on Arbitrum One. Keep some AVAX for the fee. Then hold ETH. Check Snowtrace and Arbiscan before you sign.

sections.heading: Selling AVAX can strand the source transaction
sections.body: The outbound fee is AVAX. If the quote asks for every unit the wallet shows, the fee has nowhere to come from and the signature never broadcasts. Decide the fee remainder first, then the amount you are willing to turn into dollars. X-Chain and P-Chain AVAX are not eligible. Chain id 43114 is the only network this quote can spend, and Snowtrace is where you confirm it.

sections.heading: Circle's Arbitrum USDC is a specific contract
sections.body: 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 is native USDC from Circle on Arbitrum One. Bridged USDC.e will not match a receiver who named that address, and the reverse is also true: a receiver who still wants USDC.e will reject this arrival. Tether's USDT is a third contract. Ticker-level matching is how the wrong dollar gets delivered. Arbiscan on chain id 42161 is the test.

sections.heading: USDC will not pay the first Arbitrum transaction
sections.body: Gas on Arbitrum One is ETH, not USDC and not the AVAX you just sold. Nova is not this chain. Ethereum mainnet is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan, and it will not display this USDC. Plan a little ETH on 42161 before you try to move the dollars. The sentinel address is only for native gas, never for the USDC contract.

sections.heading: A C-Chain pool is enough when Arbitrum is not the venue
sections.body: If you wanted dollars but the trade, the lender, or the payroll still lives on Avalanche, bridging to Arbitrum adds a hop you do not need. [Avalanche C-Chain](/chains/avalanche) is the network you would be leaving. Compare a local stable quote with this minimum received. Keep the better floor. Nothing on this page times the bridge.

faqs.question: Should I swap my entire AVAX balance on this route?
faqs.answer: No. AVAX at 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE pays the C-Chain fee, chain id 43114. An empty AVAX balance cannot broadcast the send. Leave a remainder, then let Circle USDC arrive on Arbitrum. Snowtrace confirms the source. X-Chain AVAX is a different system and will not fund this quote.

faqs.question: Is the USDC that arrives the bridged USDC.e token?
faqs.answer: No. The arrival is Circle's native USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. USDC.e is a different contract, and Tether USDT is another. Check Arbiscan. If your app still names the bridged token, this route is the wrong destination. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

faqs.question: Does the new USDC cover Arbitrum gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is ETH on chain id 42161, not USDC and not AVAX. Nova and Ethereum mainnet will not show this balance. Etherscan belongs to chain id 1, where blocks are about 12 seconds. Hold ETH before you move the dollars, and treat the quote minimum as the floor.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDT on Arbitrum One. Native AVAX leaves C-Chain, and Tether USDT is what can arrive on Arbitrum One.

Source gas is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. That sentinel means AVAX, and Snowtrace is the explorer. Tether on Arbitrum One is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, chain id 42161. Arbiscan has to show that contract, not Circle's USDC. You are turning a gas coin into Tether's dollar claim. ETH, not USDT, pays the fees once you arrive.
description: AVAX leaves Avalanche C-Chain and Tether USDT arrives on Arbitrum One. Keep AVAX for the fee. ETH pays gas after. Check Snowtrace and Arbiscan before you sign.

sections.heading: Tether's arrival is not Circle's USDC
sections.body: Both can trade near a dollar and still fail a transfer that names the other issuer. This route delivers Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Circle's native USDC on Arbitrum is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. If the invoice, the pool, or the custody rule says Circle, stop and use the USDC route. Arbiscan is how you prove which contract you hold after the hop.

sections.heading: The AVAX you spend is also the fee
sections.body: Because 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is native gas, there is no ERC-20 approval on the source. There is a fee in the same coin you are selling. Keep a remainder on chain id 43114. X-Chain AVAX will not appear in this wallet balance and cannot be forced through Snowtrace as a C-Chain send. If the network badge is wrong, fix that before the amount.

sections.heading: USDT on Arbitrum still needs an ETH float
sections.body: Chain id 42161 does not accept Tether as gas, and it does not accept AVAX. ETH is the fee token. Nova will not show this USDT. Ethereum, chain id 1, uses Etherscan and about 12 second blocks, and its USDT contract is a different address with its own rules. Do not budget mainnet gas out of an Arbitrum Tether balance.

sections.heading: Compare this with a stable swap that never leaves C-Chain
sections.body: If the dollars only need to exist on Avalanche, a local pool avoids the bridge, the ETH requirement, and the issuer question on Arbitrum. Cross the networks when the Tether you need is specifically the Arbitrum contract. How that handoff works is in [how cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work). The minimum received is the number you accept or you walk away from.

faqs.question: Does AVAX to Arbitrum arrive as Circle USDC?
faqs.answer: No. Native AVAX leaves C-Chain and Tether USDT at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 is what can arrive on Arbitrum One. Circle's USDC is a different contract. Confirm it on Arbiscan, chain id 42161. If the receiver requires Circle, this page is the wrong route. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Do I approve AVAX before this swap?
faqs.answer: No. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is the native gas sentinel for AVAX on chain id 43114, not an ERC-20. Snowtrace shows the send as native AVAX. You still must leave enough AVAX to pay the fee. X-Chain balances are outside this quote. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

faqs.question: Can the USDT I receive pay fees on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: No. ETH pays gas on Arbitrum One. USDT cannot, and AVAX from C-Chain cannot either. Nova is a different network. Hold a little ETH before you transfer the Tether. The quote minimum is the floor, and the bridge wait is not something this page can schedule.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on Arbitrum One. Native AVAX leaves C-Chain, and native ETH is what can arrive on Arbitrum One. Both are gas coins, on different networks.

The quote prints 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on both sides because that sentinel means native gas, not one shared asset. Outbound it is AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, checked on Snowtrace. Inbound it is ETH on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, checked on Arbiscan. It is not WETH, not Ethereum mainnet ETH, and not Arbitrum Nova.
description: AVAX leaves Avalanche C-Chain and native ETH arrives on Arbitrum One. These gas tokens are not the same balance. Check Snowtrace and Arbiscan before you sign.

sections.heading: Same sentinel, two fee coins that cannot substitute
sections.body: A wallet that still shows chain id 43114 after the transfer will keep displaying AVAX and will not reveal the ETH. Switch to 42161 and read the native ETH line. Do not import the sentinel as a token. There is no approval step for either gas coin. There is a fee in AVAX on the way out, so the amount of AVAX you sell cannot be the entire balance.

sections.heading: This ETH is not the ether on chain id 1
sections.body: Ethereum mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds and the explorer is Etherscan. Arbitrum One is an L2 with its own ETH balance for gas. Bridging AVAX here does not refill a mainnet wallet. It also does not put ETH on Base or on Nova. If a friend asked for mainnet gas, this route answers a different request. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) is the arrival network, and only that network.

sections.heading: Contracts that want WETH will reject this arrival
sections.body: WETH on Arbitrum is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Native ETH and that ERC-20 are not interchangeable until someone wraps. WBTC is a separate wrapped claim and is not native bitcoin; it is not what this quote delivers either. If the app's spend function names WETH, change routes before you sell the AVAX. Arriving in the fee coin and then wrapping is a second transaction you may not have planned.

sections.heading: X-Chain AVAX and Nova are both off this map
sections.body: C-Chain only for the source. Arbitrum One only for the destination. An X-Chain address cannot sign the EVM transaction Snowtrace would record. A Nova wallet will not show the ETH this quote can deliver. Read the minimum ETH against the AVAX you are spending. Price moves while a bridge is open, and this page does not offer a delivery clock.

faqs.question: Why does AVAX to ETH show one address twice?
faqs.answer: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE marks native gas. On Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, it is AVAX. On Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, it is ETH. Snowtrace and Arbiscan are different explorers. The balances are not the same coin, and neither one is an ERC-20 you approve. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

faqs.question: Can I use this ETH on Ethereum mainnet?
faqs.answer: No. The arrival is Arbitrum One. Ethereum is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan. Nova is not included either. AVAX left C-Chain and became L2 ETH for gas on 42161. If you needed mainnet fees, this route is the wrong destination. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

faqs.question: What if the app only accepts WETH?
faqs.answer: Use the WETH route. Native ETH from this page is the gas sentinel, not 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Wrapping later is a separate step that itself needs ETH for gas. If the contract rejects native ETH, signing this quote does not finish the job. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Arbitrum One. Native AVAX leaves C-Chain, and Arbitrum WETH is what can arrive. You receive wrapped ether, not the ETH that pays gas.

AVAX is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace treats that as native gas, not as a token approval. WETH is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Arbiscan is the explorer that can prove it. Polygon's WETH and Base's WETH are different addresses. Ethereum's WETH is different again. This page delivers only the Arbitrum contract.
description: AVAX leaves Avalanche C-Chain and WETH arrives on Arbitrum One. WETH is not the fee token. Keep ETH for gas. Check Snowtrace and Arbiscan before you sign.

sections.heading: Do not reuse a WETH address from another chain
sections.body: The contract that matters here is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Polygon WETH is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1, with about 12 second blocks and Etherscan. Pasting any of those into an Arbitrum token list does not create this balance. WBTC is not this asset either, and WBTC is not native bitcoin.

sections.heading: Native AVAX goes in, and a remainder has to stay
sections.body: There is no ERC-20 approval for the sentinel. There is an AVAX fee on chain id 43114. Selling the whole stack leaves the transaction unpaid. X-Chain AVAX cannot be substituted. Snowtrace should show native AVAX leaving a C-Chain account. If the wallet is on the wrong Avalanche network, the balance you think you have is not the balance the quote can spend.

sections.heading: WETH on arrival does not unlock the next Arbitrum action
sections.body: Gas is ETH, chain id 42161, not Nova. A WETH-only wallet still cannot transfer WETH. If you needed the fee coin, the native ETH route is the matching page. If you needed dollars, Circle USDC or Tether USDT is the matching page. Using this hop as a generic on-ramp for Arbitrum is how you land in the wrapper and then discover you cannot move it.

sections.heading: Stay home if the pool that wants WETH is not on Arbitrum
sections.body: Bridging AVAX into Arbitrum WETH, then bridging onward, pays the cross-chain cost twice. Do it when a specific Arbitrum contract calls for this WETH. The sequence of lock and release is described in [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains). Accept the minimum only when that WETH amount is the inventory you wanted.

faqs.question: Is Arbitrum WETH the same contract as Polygon WETH?
faqs.answer: No. This route delivers 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Polygon WETH is a different address on chain id 137. Check Arbiscan, not Polygonscan. AVAX left C-Chain as native gas. The wrapper you receive cannot pay Arbitrum fees. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

faqs.question: What is the AVAX address on this quote?
faqs.answer: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the native gas sentinel, on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. It is not an ERC-20 approval. Snowtrace is the explorer. X-Chain AVAX will not fund it. Leave enough AVAX to pay the outbound fee or the send cannot broadcast. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Can I skip holding ETH if I only want to keep WETH?
faqs.answer: Only if you never need to move it. Gas on Arbitrum One is ETH, and WETH is not that gas. Nova will not show this token. If the next step is a transfer or a pool deposit, hold ETH first. If you needed fees rather than the wrapper, this route is the wrong one.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to ARB on Arbitrum One. Native AVAX leaves C-Chain, and the ARB governance token is what can arrive. You sell a gas coin for a volatile token.

AVAX is quoted as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace is the source explorer. ARB is 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Arbiscan is the arrival explorer. ARB does not pay fees. ETH does. If you needed gas on Arbitrum, or dollars, this is the wrong arrival.
description: AVAX leaves Avalanche C-Chain and ARB arrives on Arbitrum One. ARB cannot pay fees. Keep ETH for gas. Check Snowtrace and Arbiscan before you sign the quote.

sections.heading: Governance exposure is the point of this page
sections.body: AVAX already moves with the market. ARB moves on its own. The route is a trade plus a bridge, not a neutral relocation of spending power. Read the minimum ARB before you give up C-Chain gas. If that floor is thin, wait for another quote or choose a stablecoin arrival. This page is wrong for anyone who asked for ETH, USDC, or USDT and then followed the ticker ARB by mistake.

sections.heading: Two gas problems, and ARB solves neither
sections.body: You must reserve AVAX on chain id 43114 to broadcast the send. You must hold ETH on chain id 42161 to move ARB after it appears. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE refers to those native coins, never to 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Nova does not use this ARB balance. A wallet full of ARB and empty of ETH is stuck.

sections.heading: Explorers split the story in half
sections.body: Snowtrace shows AVAX leaving C-Chain. It will not show ARB. Arbiscan shows ARB on Arbitrum One. It will not show your remaining AVAX. Ethereum's 12 second blocks and Etherscan belong to chain id 1 and are a third story. If you refresh the wrong explorer, a successful hop looks like a loss. Confirm the chain id in the wallet before you send a replacement transaction.

sections.heading: Prefer a fee route or a dollar route when ARB is incidental
sections.body: Buying ARB only because it is the liquid token you have heard of is a good way to hold an asset you did not mean to price. ETH is the fee top-up. Circle or Tether is the dollar arrival. Use those when they match the job. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) walks the wallet steps. The bridge itself has no promised completion time.

faqs.question: Does ARB from AVAX pay gas on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: No. ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is the governance token. Gas on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, is ETH. AVAX left C-Chain as native gas and did not become that ETH. Hold ETH before you transfer ARB. Check Arbiscan, not Nova and not Snowtrace, for the arrival.

faqs.question: Can X-Chain AVAX be the source?
faqs.answer: No. The quote spends C-Chain AVAX at 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, chain id 43114. Snowtrace is the explorer. X-Chain and P-Chain balances do not sign this EVM transaction. Leave a remainder of AVAX for the fee, because the coin you sell is also the coin that pays. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

faqs.question: When is AVAX to ARB the wrong trade?
faqs.answer: When you needed ETH for fees, Circle USDC, or Tether USDT. ARB is price exposure, not a dollar and not gas. It is also wrong if the ARB you wanted is on a network other than Arbitrum One. Read the minimum on the quote and do not sign a floor you would not hold.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on Base. Circle USDC leaves C-Chain, and native ETH is what can arrive on Base, where it pays gas on that L2.

You spend Circle at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace is the source explorer. The ETH you can receive is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the native gas sentinel, on Base, chain id 8453. Basescan shows it as ETH, not as an ERC-20. Base is an Ethereum L2, but this balance is not mainnet ETH and it is not WETH at the 0x4200 predeploy.
description: Circle USDC leaves Avalanche C-Chain and native ETH arrives on Base. Base is an L2. Pay AVAX, then hold ETH. Check Snowtrace and Basescan before you sign.

sections.heading: Base gas is ETH, and this route is how you buy it
sections.body: A Circle balance on C-Chain does not pay a Base transaction. Chain id 8453 wants ETH. The sentinel means that native coin, so you do not approve it. You also do not import it as a token. If the wallet is still on chain id 43114, you will keep staring at USDC and AVAX and miss the arrival. Switch to Base and read the ETH line on Basescan.

sections.heading: L2 ETH is not the 12 second mainnet balance
sections.body: Ethereum is chain id 1. Blocks there are about 12 seconds, and the explorer is Etherscan. Base posts data back toward Ethereum, yet the ETH in a Base account cannot cover a mainnet approval. It also cannot cover Arbitrum or Avalanche. If the empty tank is on mainnet, this page fills the wrong tank. [Base](/chains/base) is the network note for the chain you would be funding.

sections.heading: The predeploy WETH is a different job
sections.body: Base WETH sits at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Several other rollups reuse that predeploy address, and the balances are still not shared. Native ETH from this quote will not satisfy a contract that names the predeploy. WBTC is unrelated and is not native bitcoin. If the app wants wrapped ether, change to the WETH route before you approve Circle's USDC.

sections.heading: AVAX has to survive the exit
sections.body: The source fee is AVAX, not USDC. Bridged USDC.e on Avalanche is not 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. X-Chain funds do not sign this. Approve only the Circle contract the quote names. Dollar-to-ETH prices move, so treat the minimum ETH as a hard floor. A C-Chain block and a Base block do not add up to a promised delivery time.

faqs.question: Is ETH on Base the same as ETH on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Circle USDC leaves Avalanche and native ETH arrives on Base, chain id 8453, quoted as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Ethereum is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan. Basescan is the check for this arrival. The two ETH balances do not pay each other's fees. AVAX paid the source side.

faqs.question: Will this route deliver Base WETH?
faqs.answer: No. The arrival is native ETH, the gas token. WETH is the predeploy at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, and that is a different route. If a pool rejects native ETH, this page is wrong. You would still need ETH afterward to wrap. Confirm the native balance on Basescan.

faqs.question: Which USDC contract is spent on C-Chain?
faqs.answer: Circle's native USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, chain id 43114. Snowtrace is the explorer. Bridged USDC.e will not match, and X-Chain AVAX is not a source. Keep AVAX for the fee. An approval should name this Circle contract and the spender from the quote. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Base. Circle USDC leaves C-Chain, and Base WETH is what can arrive. The predeploy is wrapped ether, not the ETH you spend on gas.

Spend 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, Circle on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, and confirm the debit on Snowtrace. The WETH predeploy is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain id 8453. Basescan is the explorer. The same hex shows up as a predeploy on other rollups, but those balances are not this one. Native gas remains 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which this route does not deliver.
description: Circle USDC leaves Avalanche C-Chain and WETH arrives on Base. WETH is not gas. Pay AVAX, then hold ETH. Check Snowtrace and Basescan before you sign.

sections.heading: 0x4200 on Base is not 0x4200 on another rollup
sections.body: The predeploy address is shared by design across some Ethereum L2s. State is not. A WETH balance on Optimism, or a screenshot of that address from another chain, does not credit Base. Basescan on chain id 8453 is the only view that counts. Ethereum's canonical WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1, with about 12 second blocks and Etherscan. Importing that mainnet address here is a mistake.

sections.heading: You still need native ETH after the wrapper lands
sections.body: Base charges ETH for gas. WETH cannot pay it. If the reason you are bridging is an empty gas tank, use the native ETH route and skip this page. If a contract calls WETH specifically, this arrival matches and the gas tank is a second problem you solve with a small ETH balance. WBTC will not stand in, and WBTC is not native bitcoin.

sections.heading: Circle's C-Chain token is easy to confuse with bridged USDC
sections.body: The quote spends 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E only. USDC.e on Avalanche is a different contract and will not move. Tether will not move either. AVAX on chain id 43114 pays the approval and the send, so do not drain it. X-Chain addresses never enter Snowtrace as this transfer. Reject an approval whose spender you do not recognize from the quote.

sections.heading: Skip the hop when the WETH pool is not on Base
sections.body: Landing in Base WETH and immediately bridging to mainnet or Arbitrum pays twice for a detour. Stay on the chain that already holds the liquidity you want. The mechanism behind the two contracts is [how cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work). Take a fresh quote if the minimum WETH slips below the inventory you meant to hold. No block time on C-Chain or Base is a delivery promise.

faqs.question: Does the Base WETH predeploy exist on other chains too?
faqs.answer: The address 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is reused as a predeploy on some rollups, but the Base balance is only on chain id 8453. Another chain's copy is not yours. Circle USDC left Avalanche. Check Basescan, not Etherscan. WETH still cannot pay Base gas. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

faqs.question: Can this WETH pay fees on Base?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is native ETH, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on chain id 8453. This route delivers the wrapper, not that sentinel. Hold ETH before you transfer WETH. If you only needed fees, this page is the wrong route. AVAX on C-Chain paid the source fee. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

faqs.question: What if my Avalanche dollars are USDC.e?
faqs.answer: This quote will not spend them. It spends Circle at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, chain id 43114, which you verify on Snowtrace. Bridged USDC.e is a different contract. Move into the native Circle token first, and keep AVAX so the fee can be paid. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on Base. Tether USDT leaves C-Chain, and Circle USDC is what can arrive on Base. The issuer changes on the way across.

Tether on Avalanche is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, chain id 43114. Snowtrace is where that balance should fall. Circle's native USDC on Base is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, chain id 8453. Basescan is the arrival check. The older bridged USDbC token is not this contract. AVAX pays the exit. ETH pays every move after the USDC shows up on the L2.
description: Tether USDT leaves Avalanche C-Chain and Circle USDC arrives on Base. Pay AVAX, then hold ETH. Match both contracts on Snowtrace and Basescan before you sign.

sections.heading: Base USDC and bridged USDbC are not interchangeable
sections.body: Some older Base apps still expect USDbC. This route delivers Circle's native USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. If a pool, a vesting contract, or a deposit address names the bridged token, you will hold dollars on chain id 8453 and still be unable to deposit. Check the exact address on Basescan before you treat the hop as done. The right ticker on the right chain can still be the wrong contract.

sections.heading: The source has to be Tether, not Circle, on C-Chain
sections.body: Approving Avalanche USDC will not feed this quote. The spend is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Snowtrace should name Tether. Chain id 43114 only. An X-Chain balance is irrelevant. Keep AVAX for gas, because a stablecoin does not pay C-Chain fees. If the approval spender is unfamiliar, reject it and return to the quote.

sections.heading: An L2 dollar still needs an ETH fee balance
sections.body: Base is an Ethereum L2, chain id 8453, and gas is ETH. USDC cannot substitute. The native sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is how a quote would mark that ETH, and it is not the USDC address. Mainnet, chain id 1, uses Etherscan and about 12 second blocks. Your new USDC will not appear there. Fund a little ETH on Base before you try to forward the dollars.

sections.heading: Remain in Tether when the receiver said Tether
sections.body: Changing Circle for Tether, or the reverse, is a real decision even when both prices hug a dollar. If the Base account you are paying accepts only Tether, this Circle arrival is the wrong page. If you only needed dollars on C-Chain, do not leave. The wallet steps sit in [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains). The minimum USDC is the floor. There is no delivery timetable beside it.

faqs.question: Does this hop deliver bridged USDbC on Base?
faqs.answer: No. Tether USDT leaves Avalanche and Circle's native USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 is what can arrive on Base, chain id 8453. USDbC is a different contract. Check Basescan. If the app still names the bridged token, this route is the wrong arrival and another signature will not rename it.

faqs.question: Which Avalanche contract is spent?
faqs.answer: Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace is the explorer. Circle USDC on Avalanche is not this quote. X-Chain funds do not apply. Keep AVAX for the fee, and approve only the Tether contract the quote is using. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Will Base USDC pay the L2 gas?
faqs.answer: No. Base is an Ethereum L2 and charges ETH, not USDC and not AVAX. Chain id 8453 is the network to select. The dollars can sit unused until a small ETH balance is there. Mainnet ETH on chain id 1 will not cover it. Read the quote minimum before you sign.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on Base. Tether USDT leaves C-Chain, and native ETH is what can arrive on Base to pay L2 gas.

You send 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, Tether on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace records it. You receive the native gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which on Base, chain id 8453, means ETH. Basescan shows a native balance, not a token transfer of that sentinel. This is not the WETH predeploy, not AVAX, and not ETH on Ethereum mainnet.
description: Tether USDT leaves Avalanche C-Chain and native ETH arrives on Base. Pay AVAX, then use ETH for gas. Check Snowtrace and Basescan before you sign the quote.

sections.heading: You are refilling Base, not wrapping ether
sections.body: The sentinel is native ETH. There is nothing to approve on the destination. WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is the inventory token for contracts that refuse native ETH. If that is what the app calls, this page stops one step early and is the wrong route. If the app just needs fees, the wrapper would have been the wrong route instead. Pick from the job, not from the habit of typing WETH.

sections.heading: Tether on C-Chain is a single contract
sections.body: Circle's Avalanche USDC will not be debited. The address is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Confirm the holder on Snowtrace under chain id 43114. X-Chain AVAX and any non-C-Chain account are noise. The fee is AVAX, so converting every AVAX you hold into the bridge is how the transaction dies before Base sees it.

sections.heading: Mainnet's 12 second blocks do not describe this ETH
sections.body: Ethereum, chain id 1, uses Etherscan. Base, chain id 8453, uses Basescan. Both call the fee coin ETH. Only the Base balance pays Base. Arbitrum ETH is a third balance. [Base](/chains/base) keeps that L2 distinction in one place. A fast L2 block still does not tell you when the bridge will credit the account. Watch the address, not a timer.

sections.heading: Stay in Tether if the shortfall is not gas
sections.body: Buying ETH spends a stablecoin into a volatile price for as long as the quote and the bridge are open. If you needed Circle USDC on Base, or you needed WETH for a pool, those are different pages. Compare the minimum ETH with the dollars you are giving up. Sign only when that floor still buys the fee room you came for.

faqs.question: Is the Base arrival native ETH or the WETH predeploy?
faqs.answer: Native ETH. The quote uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Base, chain id 8453. WETH is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 and will not be credited by this route. Tether left Avalanche. Check the ETH line on Basescan, not a token import of the sentinel. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

faqs.question: Can I fund this quote with Circle USDC?
faqs.answer: No. The source is Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace should show that contract falling. Circle USDC is a different Avalanche token. Keep AVAX for the fee. X-Chain balances cannot sign the transfer. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

faqs.question: Will this ETH pay a transaction on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. It arrives on Base, an Ethereum L2, chain id 8453. Mainnet is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan. The fee coins do not merge. AVAX covered the C-Chain side only. Use the Base ETH for Base, and reject the quote if the minimum is too small for the fees you need.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Base. Tether USDT leaves C-Chain, and the Base WETH predeploy is what can arrive. Wrapped ether is not the L2 fee coin.

Spend Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, and match the exit on Snowtrace. Receive 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain id 8453, and match it on Basescan. Other rollups reuse that predeploy hex. Their WETH is not your Base balance. Native ETH stays the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which you do not receive here.
description: Tether USDT leaves Avalanche C-Chain and WETH arrives on Base. The predeploy is not gas. Pay AVAX, then hold ETH. Check Snowtrace and Basescan before you sign.

sections.heading: Inventory WETH and fee ETH are a pair, not a choice of one
sections.body: After this route you may hold WETH and still fail the deposit that needs it, because Base bills ETH. Bring a small ETH balance, or run the native ETH route first if the tank is empty. This page is the wrong one when the only goal is gas. It is the right shape when a Base contract names the predeploy and will not take raw ETH.

sections.heading: Do not trust the predeploy address on a different chain id
sections.body: 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 can exist on more than one L2. Chain id 8453 is Base. Basescan is the explorer. A balance at that address on another rollup is a different ledger. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, Etherscan. WBTC is a different wrapper and is not native bitcoin. None of those substitute for this arrival.

sections.heading: Tether has to be the C-Chain token in the quote
sections.body: Circle USDC on Avalanche will sit still. The debit is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Snowtrace, chain id 43114, X-Chain excluded. AVAX pays the network. If you spend the last AVAX, Tether never leaves and Base WETH never becomes a question. Limit the approval to the amount on the quote when the wallet offers that choice.

sections.heading: A mainnet or Arbitrum pool does not get cheaper by detouring through Base
sections.body: Cheap L2 gas does not create depth that lives somewhere else. If the book you want is on Ethereum, start there. If it is on Arbitrum, this Base WETH is the wrong inventory. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the short account of why the destination token is a new contract. Keep the minimum WETH as your line in the sand.

faqs.question: Does Base WETH from Tether pay Base gas?
faqs.answer: No. The predeploy 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is an ERC-20. Gas on Base, chain id 8453, is native ETH. Tether USDT left Avalanche C-Chain and became the wrapper. Hold ETH before you move WETH. Basescan is the explorer, and another rollup's copy of this address is not your balance.

faqs.question: What Tether contract does Avalanche spend?
faqs.answer: 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace should show Tether, not Circle. X-Chain assets are out of scope. AVAX pays the fee, so leave a remainder. An approval for a different stablecoin will not move this quote. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

faqs.question: Is this WETH the canonical contract on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1, explorer Etherscan, blocks about 12 seconds. This route credits Base only. If the pool you care about is on mainnet, bridging into the Base predeploy is the wrong job. Read the minimum before you sign. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on Base. Native AVAX leaves C-Chain, and Circle USDC is what can arrive on Base.

The source is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, native AVAX on chain id 43114, visible on Snowtrace as gas rather than as an ERC-20. Circle's USDC on Base is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, chain id 8453, visible on Basescan. That is not bridged USDbC, not Tether, and not ETH. You are selling the C-Chain fee coin, so a remainder of AVAX has to stay behind for the transaction itself.
description: AVAX leaves Avalanche C-Chain and Circle USDC arrives on Base. Keep some AVAX for the fee. Then hold ETH. Check Snowtrace and Basescan before you sign.

sections.heading: The fee and the asset are the same AVAX stack
sections.body: There is no separate approval for the sentinel. There is a fee taken from the coin you are selling. Size the trade after you reserve gas on chain id 43114. X-Chain and P-Chain AVAX never qualify, even when a portfolio view lumps all Avalanche balances together. Snowtrace on C-Chain is the record that matters. If the network in the wallet is not 43114, you are looking at a different account.

sections.heading: Circle on Base is not the legacy bridged dollar
sections.body: 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 is native USDC. USDbC is the older bridged contract, and a deposit form that still names it will reject this arrival. Tether is a different issuer again. Basescan is how you show a counterparty the exact token. Chain id 8453 must be selected or the wallet will hide a balance Basescan already confirms.

sections.heading: Dollars on an L2 do not include the gas
sections.body: Base is an Ethereum L2. Fees are ETH. USDC will not pay them, and the AVAX you sold will not pay them either. Mainnet ETH, chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, Etherscan, is yet another balance. Plan a small ETH float on Base before you forward the USDC. The gas sentinel is not the USDC address, so do not paste 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 into a fee field.

sections.heading: Keep the swap on C-Chain when Base is not the destination that asked
sections.body: A local dollar pair avoids the bridge when the receiver, the pool, or the lender is still on Avalanche. Cross to Base when someone named this Circle contract. [Avalanche C-Chain](/chains/avalanche) is the side you are spending down. Compare minimum USDC with a stay-at-home quote and keep the one that preserves more of the dollar. The bridge does not publish a finish time.

faqs.question: Should the whole AVAX balance go to Base USDC?
faqs.answer: No. AVAX at 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE pays the fee on C-Chain, chain id 43114. Spending all of it stops the broadcast. Leave a remainder, then let Circle USDC arrive on Base. Snowtrace confirms the source. X-Chain AVAX cannot be used in its place. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

faqs.question: Is Base USDC the same as bridged USDbC?
faqs.answer: No. This route delivers Circle at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on chain id 8453. USDbC is a different contract, and Tether is a different issuer. Check Basescan. If the form you are filling still asks for the bridged token, this arrival will not satisfy it. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Does the USDC pay gas on Base?
faqs.answer: No. Base is an Ethereum L2 and charges ETH, chain id 8453. USDC cannot pay that fee, and AVAX from C-Chain cannot either. Hold ETH before you move the dollars. Mainnet gas on chain id 1 is a separate ETH balance, checked on Etherscan, not on Basescan.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on Base. Native AVAX leaves C-Chain, and native ETH is what can arrive on Base. You trade one gas coin for the L2 gas coin.

Both sides print 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE because that sentinel means native gas, not a shared token. Leaving, it is AVAX on chain id 43114, which Snowtrace shows. Arriving, it is ETH on Base, chain id 8453, which Basescan shows. Base is an Ethereum L2. This ETH is not mainnet ETH, not WETH, and not AVAX that somehow became portable.
description: AVAX leaves Avalanche C-Chain and native ETH arrives on Base. Both are gas tokens on different chains. Check Snowtrace and Basescan before you sign it.

sections.heading: Two native balances hide behind one sentinel
sections.body: Do not import 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE as an ERC-20 on either side. There is no approval. There is a fee in AVAX, so the amount you bridge cannot empty the C-Chain account. After the hop, change the wallet from chain id 43114 to 8453 before you decide the ETH is missing. X-Chain AVAX was never in this quote.

sections.heading: L2 ETH will not clear a mainnet transaction
sections.body: Ethereum, chain id 1, takes about 12 seconds per block and uses Etherscan. Base uses Basescan. A request for mainnet gas is a different bridge, to a different chain id. Arbitrum ETH is different again. [Base](/chains/base) is only the arrival you get from this page. If the empty wallet is on mainnet, stop here.

sections.heading: The predeploy wants a different route
sections.body: Contracts that call 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 want WETH, not the native ETH this quote delivers.
