Wrapping is possible later, and wrapping itself costs ETH, so arriving in the fee coin is not useless. It is incomplete when the function selector expects the predeploy. WBTC is not a stand-in, and it is not native bitcoin. Switch routes if the ABI names WETH.

sections.heading: Price the gas you are buying, then stop
sections.body: AVAX and ETH both move. The minimum ETH on the quote is the only floor you can enforce. If you needed dollars on Base, a USDC route avoids turning spending money into a volatile coin you must sell again. C-Chain confirmation is not the moment Base credits you. This page will not name a fill time. Refresh Basescan for the destination address instead of refreshing a clock.

faqs.question: Why is the address identical for AVAX and Base ETH?
faqs.answer: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means native gas. On Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, that is AVAX, checked on Snowtrace. On Base, chain id 8453, that is ETH, checked on Basescan. The coins are not interchangeable, and neither is an ERC-20 you approve. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

faqs.question: Can this ETH pay Ethereum mainnet fees?
faqs.answer: No. It arrives on Base, an Ethereum L2. Mainnet is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan. Those ETH balances do not mix. AVAX left C-Chain and became Base gas only. If you needed mainnet fees, this route points at the wrong chain.

faqs.question: What if I needed WETH on Base instead?
faqs.answer: Use the WETH route. Native ETH will not satisfy the predeploy at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 until you wrap, and wrapping needs ETH for gas. If the contract accepts only the wrapper, this page is the wrong arrival. Basescan is where you would later confirm the predeploy balance.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Base. Native AVAX leaves C-Chain, and Base WETH is what can arrive. The predeploy is an ERC-20, not the ETH that pays gas.

AVAX is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace shows native gas leaving. WETH is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain id 8453. Basescan is the check. That hex is a common predeploy, so a balance on another rollup is not this balance. You do not receive native ETH, and you do not receive WBTC.
description: AVAX leaves Avalanche C-Chain and WETH arrives on Base. The predeploy cannot pay gas. Keep ETH on Base. Check Snowtrace and Basescan before you sign it.

sections.heading: A shared predeploy hex is not a shared balance
sections.body: Seeing 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on another L2 does not credit chain id 8453. Basescan is the only explorer for this arrival. Arbitrum WETH is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, a completely different address. Polygon WETH is different again. Ethereum's WETH, 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, lives on chain id 1 with about 12 second blocks and Etherscan. Paste the Base predeploy only.

sections.heading: Leave AVAX for the C-Chain fee
sections.body: The sentinel is not an approval target. It is the coin that also pays the network. Drain it and the swap never broadcasts. X-Chain AVAX is the wrong chain inside Avalanche, not a backup balance. Snowtrace on 43114 should show the debit from a C-Chain account. If the wallet network is off, fix it before you type the amount you are willing to sell.

sections.heading: WETH on Base cannot start the next transaction
sections.body: Gas is ETH. Base is an L2, and the fee is still ETH, not AVAX and not the wrapper. If you are bridging because a button said insufficient funds, read whether it wanted ETH or WETH. The native route answers the first. This page answers the second. Arriving in WETH with an empty ETH line recreates the error you were trying to clear.

sections.heading: Do not detour through Base for a pool that lives elsewhere
sections.body: If the contract you must call is on Ethereum or Arbitrum, Base WETH is the wrong inventory. Bridge only when this predeploy is the token the app named. The steps are in [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains). Judge the minimum WETH, not a guessed wait. WBTC is a separate claim on bitcoin and is not what Avalanche is selling into here.

faqs.question: Is Base WETH the same token as WETH on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: No. This route delivers 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain id 8453. Arbitrum WETH is a different contract on chain id 42161. Check Basescan. AVAX left C-Chain as native gas. The wrapper cannot pay Base fees, so hold ETH as well. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

faqs.question: Do I approve AVAX before it leaves?
faqs.answer: No. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is native AVAX on chain id 43114, not an ERC-20. Snowtrace shows the send. X-Chain balances do not qualify. Leave enough AVAX to pay the fee, because the asset you sell is also the asset that pays for the transaction. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

faqs.question: When should I avoid AVAX to Base WETH?
faqs.answer: When you needed native ETH for gas, Circle USDC, or a WETH contract on another chain. The predeploy on a different rollup is not this balance. Ethereum mainnet WETH is chain id 1 and uses Etherscan. If the pool is not on Base, this hop is the wrong job. Read the minimum first.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to USDT on Solana. Circle USDC leaves C-Chain, and Tether's SPL mint is what can arrive on Solana. The wallet has to change with the account model.

You spend 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, Circle's ERC-20 on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace is the source explorer, and an approval can exist on that contract. The USDT you want is the SPL mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Solscan is the explorer. Phantom or Solflare can hold it. MetaMask cannot. Solana does not use an ERC-20 approval for that mint.
description: Circle USDC leaves Avalanche C-Chain and Tether USDT arrives on Solana. Use Phantom, not MetaMask. Check Snowtrace and Solscan before you sign the hop.

sections.heading: An ERC-20 approval stops at the C-Chain door
sections.body: Circle's token on Avalanche can ask for approve. That call is an EVM action on chain id 43114, paid in AVAX. It does not authorize anything inside Phantom. On Solana the USDT mint is held in a token account, and there is no ERC-20 approval to revoke afterward. If a browser wallet still looks like MetaMask when you expect the USDT, you are watching the wrong account model. [Solana](/chains/solana) is the arrival network, and it is not an extra Avalanche chain id.

sections.heading: Tether's mint is not Circle's mint
sections.body: Solana USDC from Circle is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. This route does not deliver it. It delivers Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. A payroll or a pool that names the Circle mint will reject Tether even though both are called dollars. If you needed to keep Circle, this page is the wrong route. Solscan is where the mint address has to match character for character.

sections.heading: C-Chain rules still apply on the way out
sections.body: X-Chain AVAX will not pay the fee, and USDC.e is not 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. Snowtrace should show Circle's native contract declining. Leave AVAX in the EVM wallet. The Solana side needs its own fee payer in SOL, which this USDT arrival does not provide. A brand new Phantom wallet with zero SOL cannot move the mint it just received.

sections.heading: Do not paste an SPL mint into an Ethereum field
sections.body: Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB is not a 0x address. A form that demands 42 hex characters is still on an EVM chain. Sending this quote's destination into that form will not create USDT. Stay on Solana for the credit, and stay on C-Chain for the debit. The minimum on the quote is the floor. Neither Snowtrace nor Solscan will give you a bridge timetable.

faqs.question: Can MetaMask hold the USDT from this route?
faqs.answer: No. Tether arrives as the SPL mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, which Phantom or Solflare can hold. MetaMask is the wallet for the Circle USDC you spend on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Solscan, not Snowtrace, shows the mint. There is no ERC-20 approval on the Solana side.

faqs.question: Is the arrival Circle's USDC on Solana?
faqs.answer: No. Circle leaves Avalanche at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E and Tether's mint is what can arrive. Circle's Solana USDC is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, a different mint. If the receiver named that Circle mint, this route is wrong. Confirm the mint on Solscan before you rely on it. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

faqs.question: What pays fees on each side?
faqs.answer: AVAX pays on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, and you check that on Snowtrace. SOL pays on Solana, and USDT cannot replace it. A Phantom wallet with the mint and no SOL still cannot transfer. X-Chain AVAX is not the source. Keep both fee coins in mind before you sign the quote.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to SOL on Solana. Circle USDC leaves C-Chain, and SOL is what can arrive, identified by the wrapped SOL mint that SPL programs use.

The dollars you spend are 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace can show an ERC-20 approval and the debit. The quote names SOL as So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. That is the wrapped SOL mint, not an Ethereum contract and not the native gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Solscan is the explorer. Phantom holds it. Fees on Solana are native SOL.
description: Circle USDC leaves Avalanche C-Chain and SOL arrives on Solana. The quote uses the wrapped SOL mint. Check Snowtrace and Solscan before you sign the hop.

sections.heading: So111 is the mint, and native SOL is the fee
sections.body: SPL routes point at So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 when the asset is SOL. That mint is how programs move SOL as a token. The fee payer is still native SOL in the wallet. If this hop is your first SOL, you can receive a balance you cannot spend until a little native SOL exists to pay rent and fees. Buying SOL and having zero spendable fee is a real outcome, not a failed explorer refresh.

sections.heading: There is no ERC-20 approval on the Solana side
sections.body: Any approve screen belongs to Circle's contract on C-Chain, paid in AVAX. Phantom will not ask you to approve an ERC-20 for the mint. MetaMask cannot display So111 as a normal token balance. If you paste the mint into a 0x field, the field is the wrong chain. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the sequence. The Solana account model is the part people skip.

sections.heading: This page is wrong when you wanted to stay in dollars
sections.body: Circle on Solana is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Tether is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Neither mint is the destination here. If a merchant invoices USDC, converting to SOL adds price risk you did not need. If you already hold SOL and only needed more Circle dollars on C-Chain, you are traveling the wrong direction entirely.

sections.heading: C-Chain still has to be chain id 43114
sections.body: USDC.e will not match 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. X-Chain AVAX will not pay the exit. Snowtrace is the debit explorer. Solscan is the credit explorer. Do not expect one search bar to show both. The minimum SOL is the floor. A C-Chain confirmation does not schedule the moment the mint appears.

faqs.question: Is So111 native gas the way 0xEeee is on Avalanche?
faqs.answer: No. So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is the wrapped SOL mint SPL programs use. Native SOL pays Solana fees. On Avalanche the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is AVAX, chain id 43114. Solscan shows the mint. Phantom holds it. There is no ERC-20 approval for that mint. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

faqs.question: Will MetaMask show the SOL from this swap?
faqs.answer: No. The arrival is an SPL mint, and MetaMask does not hold it. Circle USDC leaves from 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on C-Chain, which an EVM wallet can spend. Use Phantom or Solflare for the SOL. Check Solscan for So111, and keep a little native SOL for fees after it arrives.

faqs.question: Should I use this if the invoice says USDC?
faqs.answer: No. This route turns Circle dollars into SOL. Solana USDC is the mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, which you are not receiving. Tether is a different mint again. If the receiver wants a dollar token, this page is the wrong arrival. Read the minimum SOL only if SOL is what you meant to hold.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on Solana. Tether USDT leaves C-Chain, and Circle's SPL mint is what can arrive on Solana.

The source contract is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, Tether on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace is the EVM explorer, and AVAX pays the fee. Circle on Solana is the mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Solscan is where that mint has to match. Phantom can hold the token account. There is no ERC-20 approval once the asset is on Solana. MetaMask cannot be the receiving wallet.
description: Tether USDT leaves Avalanche C-Chain and Circle USDC arrives on Solana. Phantom holds the mint. Check Snowtrace and Solscan before you sign the quote.

sections.heading: Issuer and account model change in the same hop
sections.body: You leave Tether's ERC-20 and arrive in Circle's SPL mint. A receiver who asked for Tether on Solana wanted Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, and this page will not deliver it. A receiver who asked for Circle on Avalanche never needed Solana. Use this route only when the destination mint is specifically EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Solscan is the proof, not a ticker search.

sections.heading: The approval, if any, is only on Tether's C-Chain contract
sections.body: Chain id 43114, Snowtrace, AVAX for gas. X-Chain is irrelevant. Do not approve Circle's Avalanche USDC and expect this quote to spend it. On the far side, Phantom does not show an ERC-20 allowance to revoke. That absence is normal. What you need instead is a little native SOL so the new token account can move. USDC itself will not pay Solana fees.

sections.heading: Do not treat the mint as a hex address
sections.body: EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v will not validate in an Ethereum address box. The native gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is an EVM idea and is not how Solana marks SOL. If your destination form is a 0x field, you are still on Base, Arbitrum, or C-Chain, and this USDC will not land there. Switch the receiving wallet, not just a network dropdown inside MetaMask.

sections.heading: A same-chain stable swap wins when you are not leaving
sections.body: Tether and Circle both exist on C-Chain. If the dollars never needed to become an SPL mint, bridging is the long way around. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) explains why the destination mint is a different object from the source contract. Compare the minimum USDC with a local quote. There is no clock on the bridge to make a thin minimum acceptable.

faqs.question: Does this route deliver Tether's Solana mint?
faqs.answer: No. Tether leaves Avalanche at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 and Circle's mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v is what can arrive. Tether on Solana is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. If that is the mint your app named, this page is wrong. Check Solscan, and hold the token in Phantom. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Is there an ERC-20 approval on Solana?
faqs.answer: No. Solana USDC is an SPL mint, and Phantom does not use ERC-20 approvals. Any approval you sign is on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, against Tether, paid in AVAX. Snowtrace is that explorer. After arrival you need a little native SOL for fees, because the USDC mint will not pay them.

faqs.question: Can I receive this USDC in MetaMask?
faqs.answer: No. MetaMask can spend the Avalanche Tether. It cannot hold EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Use Phantom or Solflare and confirm the mint on Solscan. Pasting the mint into a 0x address field will not create the balance. Keep SOL for the next Solana transaction. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to SOL on Solana. Tether USDT leaves C-Chain, and SOL is what can arrive, quoted as the wrapped SOL mint.

Tether is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Snowtrace shows that ERC-20, and AVAX pays the fee. The destination mint is So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. Solscan is the explorer. That mint is how SPL programs represent SOL. It is not native fee SOL by itself, and it is not an EVM address. Phantom holds it. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana.
description: Tether USDT leaves Avalanche C-Chain and SOL arrives on Solana. The mint is wrapped SOL. Phantom holds it. Check Snowtrace and Solscan before you sign.

sections.heading: Wrapped SOL on the quote, native SOL for the fee
sections.body: So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is the mint in the route. Fees and account rent want native SOL in the paying account. A first-time Phantom wallet can show the mint and still fail the next click. This route is a way to obtain SOL, and it does not guarantee a separate fee cushion beyond what arrives. If you already have SOL and only needed Tether to stay Tether, you are converting a dollar into a volatile coin for nothing.

sections.heading: Circle's mint and Tether's mint are the dollar alternatives
sections.body: If the Solana balance you lack is USDC, the mint is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v and this page is wrong. If it is USDT, the mint is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB and this page is also wrong. SOL is the right arrival only when you intend to hold SOL or to pay Solana fees. Price that decision off the minimum on the quote, not off the word swap.

sections.heading: The EVM half still has Avalanche's constraints
sections.body: Chain id 43114 only. Tether only, not Circle's C-Chain USDC. X-Chain excluded. Snowtrace for the debit. An approval, if the wallet raises one, spends AVAX and ends at the bridge. It does not create an allowance Phantom must later revoke. [Solana](/chains/solana) describes the wallet side you are entering. MetaMask's network list has no switch that turns it into Phantom.

sections.heading: Never drop So111 into a hex address box
sections.body: The mint uses Solana's base58 format. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is Avalanche gas, not a Solana concept. A withdrawal form from an exchange that wants an ERC-20 address will reject or misread this destination. Send to a Solana address you control in Phantom, then confirm the mint on Solscan. The bridge wait is not a number this page will invent.

faqs.question: What does the So111 mint mean on this route?
faqs.answer: So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is the wrapped SOL mint SPL programs use to represent SOL. Native SOL still pays fees. Tether left Avalanche at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Check the mint on Solscan and hold it in Phantom. It is not an Ethereum contract and not the 0xEeee gas sentinel. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

faqs.question: Do I revoke an approval on Solana afterward?
faqs.answer: No. There is no ERC-20 approval on the SPL side. Any approval you signed was against Tether on C-Chain, chain id 43114, and Snowtrace is where that lives. AVAX paid it. Phantom will not show an allowance. You do need native SOL later so the wallet can pay Solana fees.

faqs.question: Is this the route for Circle USDC on Solana?
faqs.answer: No. The arrival is SOL, not Circle's mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v and not Tether's mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. If a dollar token is what the other side asked for, this page is the wrong conversion. Read the minimum SOL only when you want the exposure. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on Solana. Native AVAX leaves C-Chain, and Circle's SPL mint is what can arrive on Solana.

AVAX is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the native gas sentinel, on chain id 43114. Snowtrace shows it as gas, with no ERC-20 approval. Circle on Solana is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Solscan is the mint check. Phantom or Solflare holds the token account. MetaMask does not. You are selling the C-Chain fee coin, so the amount has to leave AVAX behind for the send.
description: AVAX leaves Avalanche C-Chain and Circle USDC arrives on Solana. Keep AVAX for the fee. Phantom holds the mint. Check Snowtrace and Solscan before you sign.

sections.heading: Selling AVAX and receiving an SPL mint are different wallets
sections.body: The signature that spends AVAX happens in an EVM wallet on chain id 43114. The USDC that can arrive lives in a Solana token account. Watching MetaMask after you sign will not reveal EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Open Phantom and Solscan. There is no network dropdown that makes those the same account. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is worth reading if this is the first time the wallet family changes.

sections.heading: Circle's Solana mint is not Tether and not C-Chain USDC
sections.body: Tether on Solana is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. If the app named that mint, this route is wrong. Circle's ERC-20 on Avalanche, 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, is also a different object from the SPL mint, even though both are Circle. You cannot spend the Avalanche contract from Phantom, and you cannot import the mint as that contract on Snowtrace.

sections.heading: Reserve AVAX, then reserve SOL
sections.body: The source fee is the coin you are selling. Leave a remainder on C-Chain or the transaction cannot broadcast. X-Chain AVAX is not a substitute. On Solana, the USDC mint does not pay fees. A Phantom wallet that has only the new USDC and no SOL cannot transfer it. This route does not deliver the wrapped SOL mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. Budget a little SOL separately if the destination wallet is empty.

sections.heading: Stay on C-Chain when the dollar never needed Solana
sections.body: Local pools can turn AVAX into Circle or Tether without an SPL mint, a second wallet, or a bridge wait. Use this page when a Solana program named EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. The minimum USDC is the floor. Snowtrace will not show the credit, and Solscan will not show the remaining AVAX. No one should treat those explorers as a timer.

faqs.question: Which wallet receives the Solana USDC?
faqs.answer: Phantom or Solflare, not MetaMask. The mint is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, checked on Solscan. AVAX leaves C-Chain as native gas at 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, chain id 43114. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana. Keep a little SOL so the token account can move. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

faqs.question: Is this the same Circle USDC I hold on Avalanche?
faqs.answer: No. Avalanche Circle is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, an ERC-20 on Snowtrace. This route sells AVAX, not that contract, and the arrival is the Solana mint. They share an issuer and not a balance. If you needed the C-Chain token, do not bridge. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

faqs.question: What if I needed Tether on Solana instead?
faqs.answer: Then this page is wrong. Tether's mint is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, and Circle's mint will not satisfy a program that names it. Switch routes before you sell AVAX. Leave enough AVAX on chain id 43114 for the fee, and confirm whichever mint you do receive on Solscan.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDT on Solana. Native AVAX leaves C-Chain, and Tether's SPL mint is what can arrive on Solana.

The AVAX sentinel is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 43114. Snowtrace shows native gas, not an approval. Tether on Solana is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Solscan is the explorer for that mint. Phantom holds the token account. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana, and MetaMask cannot be where you look for the credit. Keep AVAX for the C-Chain fee.
description: AVAX leaves Avalanche C-Chain and Tether USDT arrives on Solana. Keep AVAX for the fee. Phantom holds the mint. Check Snowtrace and Solscan before you sign.

sections.heading: Tether's mint is the whole point of the arrival
sections.body: Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB is not Circle's EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Programs that settle in Circle will ignore a Tether balance, and the reverse is true. This page is the wrong route when the Solana instruction names the Circle mint. It is also the wrong route when you wanted SOL itself, which is the wrapped mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, not a dollar.

sections.heading: The source wallet and the destination wallet are not a network toggle
sections.body: Spending AVAX is an EVM signature on C-Chain. Receiving the mint is a Solana account. MetaMask can do the first and cannot do the second. Phantom can do the second and cannot sign chain id 43114 as if it were an Ethereum chain. [Solana](/chains/solana) is the side you are entering. Solscan will not index your leftover AVAX, and Snowtrace will not index the mint.

sections.heading: Fee coins on both ends, and USDT is neither
sections.body: Leave AVAX on chain id 43114 or the send never broadcasts. X-Chain is the wrong Avalanche chain. On Solana, hold native SOL or the new Tether cannot move. The route does not deliver the gas sentinel as a Solana concept. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE stops being meaningful the moment you are looking at Phantom. Plan the SOL fee before you need to forward the mint.

sections.heading: A C-Chain stable is quieter if Solana was optional
sections.body: AVAX to Tether can be done on C-Chain when the creditor, the pool, or your own books are still there. Cross only for the SPL mint. The minimum USDT is the number that matters. A thin quote can cost more than the AVAX fee you were trying to escape. This page does not turn a block on either chain into an arrival time.

faqs.question: Does AVAX arrive as Circle USDC on Solana?
faqs.answer: No. Native AVAX leaves C-Chain and Tether's mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB is what can arrive. Circle's mint is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Check Solscan and hold the token in Phantom. If the program wants Circle, this route is the wrong mint. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Do I approve the AVAX sentinel first?
faqs.answer: No. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is native gas on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, shown on Snowtrace. There is no ERC-20 approval for it, and there is none on Solana either. Leave enough AVAX to pay the fee. X-Chain balances cannot sign this send. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

faqs.question: Why can Phantom show USDT and still fail a transfer?
faqs.answer: Because Solana fees are native SOL, and the USDT mint does not pay them. A new wallet can hold Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB and have nothing for rent or fees. Fund a little SOL before you move the mint. MetaMask will not show this balance at all. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to SOL on Solana. Native AVAX leaves C-Chain, and SOL is what can arrive, identified by the wrapped SOL mint.

Both assets are gas coins in their own worlds, and they are not the same kind of address. AVAX is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 43114, checked on Snowtrace. SOL is So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, the wrapped mint, checked on Solscan. Native SOL pays Solana fees. Phantom holds the account. There is no ERC-20 approval on that side, and an X-Chain AVAX balance cannot start the hop.
description: AVAX leaves Avalanche C-Chain and SOL arrives on Solana. One is EVM gas, the other an SPL mint. Check Snowtrace and Solscan before you sign this hop now.

sections.heading: A gas coin does not travel as itself
sections.body: AVAX on C-Chain cannot pay a Solana fee, and SOL cannot pay chain id 43114. The quote converts one into the other through a bridge, it does not teleport a balance. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE has no meaning inside Phantom. So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 has no meaning inside an Ethereum token list. If you paste either address into the other chain's form, you are done looking at the wrong system.

sections.heading: Wrapped mint versus the SOL that pays
sections.body: The route names the wrapped SOL mint because that is how SPL programs refer to SOL. Fees want native SOL. Landing with wrapped SOL and an empty fee payer is a stuck wallet, not a missing transaction. This page is the wrong one if you needed Circle's mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v or Tether's mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Those are dollar claims. This is SOL exposure.

sections.heading: Leave C-Chain AVAX, then open a different wallet
sections.body: Reserve AVAX for the source fee. X-Chain and P-Chain do not sign it. Snowtrace confirms the debit on 43114. Then look at Phantom, not at a network switch in MetaMask. [Solana](/chains/solana) is the arrival. Solscan confirms the mint. MetaMask remaining on Avalanche will look like the funds vanished when they are simply not an ERC-20 anymore.

sections.heading: Skip the bridge when both trades can live on one chain
sections.body: If you need SOL-priced exposure that already has a market on C-Chain, or AVAX exposure that already has a market on Solana, a local pool may be the smaller job. Cross when you specifically need the mint So111 on Solana or you are done with C-Chain gas. Read the minimum SOL. Neither chain's block cadence is a promise about when the other wallet updates.

faqs.question: Are AVAX and SOL the same kind of gas address?
faqs.answer: No. AVAX is the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on C-Chain, chain id 43114, explorer Snowtrace. SOL on this quote is the wrapped mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, explorer Solscan. Native SOL pays Solana fees. Phantom holds it. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

faqs.question: Can I send X-Chain AVAX to buy SOL?
faqs.answer: No. This quote spends C-Chain AVAX only. X-Chain and P-Chain balances do not sign the EVM transaction. Switch to chain id 43114, leave a fee remainder, and confirm the debit on Snowtrace. The SOL credit, if it comes, is visible in Phantom and on Solscan, not in that C-Chain view.

faqs.question: What if I needed USDC on Solana rather than SOL?
faqs.answer: Use a USDC route. Circle's mint is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, and this page delivers SOL instead. Tether is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Selling AVAX into the wrong mint is expensive to unwind. Read the minimum only after the destination asset is the one you meant. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

intro:
Swap USDC from Solana to USDT on Ethereum. Circle's SPL mint leaves Solana, and Tether's ERC-20 is what can arrive on Ethereum mainnet.

You send EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v from a Solana token account. Solscan is the explorer, Phantom or Solflare signs, and there is no ERC-20 approval on that mint. You are aiming at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, Tether on Ethereum, chain id 1. Etherscan is the check. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. That USDT does not pay gas. ETH does, and a mainnet wallet with only USDT still cannot move it.
description: Circle USDC leaves Solana and Tether USDT arrives on Ethereum. Gas is SOL, then ETH. Check Solscan and Etherscan before you sign the quote. Read the minimum.

sections.heading: Mainnet USDT is six decimals and fussy about allowances
sections.body: 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 uses six decimals, unlike some pegged USDT contracts that use eighteen. A raw unit copied from another chain will look enormous or tiny. Tether's mainnet contract also often refuses a new approval until the old allowance is set back to zero. That quirk appears only after the USDT has arrived and you try to spend it. It is not part of the Solana send. If your spender is stuck, reset the allowance before you raise it again.

sections.heading: Circle on Ethereum is a different contract
sections.body: If the receiver wanted USDC, the address is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, and this route is wrong. Maker DAI is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F, also wrong for this page. Tether is the arrival you get. Etherscan on chain id 1 is the proof. A Base or Arbitrum USDT balance is a third mistake. Do not tell a counterparty the funds are on mainnet until that exact contract shows the credit.

sections.heading: Phantom signs the debit, an EVM wallet must receive
sections.body: MetaMask cannot hold EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, and Phantom cannot hold the Ethereum USDT. You need both wallets funded for fees: native SOL on the way out, ETH on the way in. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is that ETH, not the USDT. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is the arrival network. Leaving SOL at zero strands the source signature the same way leaving ETH at zero strands the destination.

sections.heading: Stay on Solana when the dollar never needed mainnet
sections.body: Circle and Tether both have Solana mints. A local swap avoids Ethereum gas, the 12 second blocks, and the allowance quirk. Bridge when the creditor named 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. The minimum USDT is the floor. Solscan confirming the burn or lock is not the moment Etherscan must update, and this page will not pretend there is a fixed gap between them.

faqs.question: Does Solana USDC arrive as USDC on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Circle's mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v leaves Solana and Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is what can arrive on Ethereum, chain id 1. Circle's mainnet USDC is a different contract. Check Etherscan. If the receiver said Circle, this route is wrong. ETH is still required to move the USDT.

faqs.question: Why might a later USDT approval fail?
faqs.answer: Tether on Ethereum often requires the allowance to be reset to zero before a new approval. That behavior belongs to 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, and it is not an ERC-20 step on Solana. Phantom does not approve the SPL mint that way. Check the allowance on Etherscan, and keep ETH for the reset.

faqs.question: What pays gas on each side of this hop?
faqs.answer: Native SOL pays on Solana, and you confirm the mint on Solscan with Phantom. ETH pays on Ethereum, chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan. USDT cannot pay that fee. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE marks ETH, not Tether. Hold both fee coins before you sign.

intro:
Swap USDC from Solana to DAI on Ethereum. Circle's SPL mint leaves Solana, and Maker DAI is what can arrive on Ethereum. You change issuer, not just chain.

The mint you send is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Solscan shows it, Phantom signs it, and there is no ERC-20 approval on Solana. DAI on Ethereum is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F, chain id 1, checked on Etherscan. Blocks are about 12 seconds. DAI is Maker's crypto-backed dollar, not Circle and not Tether. It does not pay gas. ETH does.
description: Circle USDC leaves Solana and Maker DAI arrives on Ethereum. DAI is not Circle. Pay SOL, then ETH. Check Solscan and Etherscan before you sign. Read the floor.

sections.heading: Maker DAI is not a renamed USDC
sections.body: Circle's mainnet USDC is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. This route delivers neither. A treasury rule that says Circle or Tether will reject DAI even when the price is near a dollar. DAI is backed by collateral inside Maker's system, and that design is the reason some desks want it and others forbid it. If your receiver named a different dollar, this page is the wrong arrival.

sections.heading: Twelve second blocks are not the bridge
sections.body: Ethereum, chain id 1, produces blocks in about 12 seconds. That cadence describes mainnet, not the wait between Solscan and Etherscan. Phantom can show the USDC gone while the EVM wallet still shows no DAI. Do not resend because the second explorer is quiet. Resending spends another mint balance. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where the DAI contract lives, and only Etherscan can show 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F.

sections.heading: Two wallets, two fee coins
sections.body: Native SOL pays the Solana side. There is no approve() call to revoke in Phantom. ETH, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, pays every mainnet move of the DAI after it lands. A wallet that receives DAI and holds no ETH cannot transfer it, vote with it, or sell it. MetaMask cannot watch the SPL mint, and Phantom cannot watch the DAI. Plan both before you sign.

sections.heading: Keep Circle if the only goal was mainnet USDC
sections.body: Crossing issuers adds a risk you can avoid. If the Ethereum account needs Circle, use a USDC route. If it needs Tether, use a USDT route. If the dollars can stay on Solana, do not touch mainnet gas at all. The minimum DAI is the floor. A quote that converts too much Circle into too little DAI should be refused, no matter how familiar both tickers look.

faqs.question: Is DAI from this route Circle USDC or Tether?
faqs.answer: Neither. Circle's mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v leaves Solana and Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is what can arrive on Ethereum, chain id 1. Check Etherscan. If the desk only accepts Circle or Tether, this route is wrong. DAI also cannot pay mainnet gas. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

faqs.question: Does Phantom approve the USDC like an ERC-20?
faqs.answer: No. The Solana mint has no ERC-20 approval. Phantom or Solflare signs a Solana transaction, and Solscan is the explorer. Any approve screen you see later is on Ethereum, against DAI, paid in ETH. Keep native SOL for the source fee so the mint can leave in the first place.

faqs.question: Will the DAI show up in the same wallet that held USDC?
faqs.answer: No. The USDC was an SPL mint. The DAI is an ERC-20 on chain id 1. MetaMask or another EVM wallet has to receive it, and that wallet needs ETH. About 12 second blocks describe Ethereum, not the bridge wait. Do not resend while Etherscan is still quiet.

intro:
Swap USDC from Solana to ETH on Ethereum. Circle's SPL mint leaves Solana, and native ETH is what can arrive on Ethereum mainnet, where it pays gas.

You spend EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Solscan and Phantom handle that mint, with no ERC-20 approval. The arrival is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the native gas sentinel, on chain id 1. Etherscan shows ETH, not a token transfer of the sentinel. This is not WETH, not Base ETH, and not Arbitrum ETH. Blocks on mainnet are about 12 seconds, which still does not time the bridge.
description: Circle USDC leaves Solana and native ETH arrives on Ethereum. That ETH pays mainnet gas. Check Solscan and Etherscan before you sign the quote. Read the floor.

sections.heading: You are buying the mainnet fee coin
sections.body: A Solana dollar balance cannot pay an Ethereum transaction. This route exists to turn Circle's mint into ETH on chain id 1. You do not approve the sentinel. You receive native ETH. If a token importer asks you to add 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, close it and read the ETH row. WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is a different route for contracts that refuse native ETH.

sections.heading: L2 ETH will not be credited
sections.body: Base and Arbitrum also call their fee coin ETH. Their chain ids are 8453 and 42161. This page does not fill them. If a friend asked for gas on Base, sending this route leaves you with mainnet ETH and their wallet still empty. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the general sequence. The chain id in the receiving wallet has to be 1 before the balance is meaningful.

sections.heading: Keep SOL back, and do not expect USDC to subsidize it
sections.body: Native SOL pays the Solana transaction. Spending every SOL and then wondering why Phantom will not sign is the mirror of spending every ETH on mainnet. Circle's mint does not pay either fee. MetaMask cannot display EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. After the hop, the ETH you bought is the fee cushion for whatever you do next on Etherscan's chain.

sections.heading: A dollar route is calmer when you do not need gas
sections.body: ETH moves while the quote is open. If the Ethereum asset you needed was USDT, DAI, or WETH, this native arrival is the wrong shape. If you only needed more SOL fees, you should not be leaving Solana at all. Read the minimum ETH against the Circle you are spending. Refuse a floor that does not buy the gas room you came for.

faqs.question: Is the ETH from Solana USDC the WETH contract?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH arrives, quoted as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Ethereum, chain id 1. WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Circle's mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v left Solana. Check the ETH line on Etherscan. If a contract wants the wrapper, this route is wrong. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Can this ETH pay fees on Base or Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: No. It arrives on Ethereum mainnet, chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan. Base is 8453 and Arbitrum One is 42161. Those ETH balances are separate. SOL paid the source fee in Phantom. Use this ETH only for mainnet, and do not import the gas sentinel as a token.

faqs.question: Does the Solana side use an ERC-20 approval?
faqs.answer: No. USDC there is an SPL mint, and Phantom does not approve it the Ethereum way. Solscan is the source explorer. Keep native SOL so the transaction can be signed. The destination fee is ETH, which this route is trying to buy, so size the minimum with that use in mind.

intro:
Swap USDC from Solana to WETH on Ethereum. Circle's SPL mint leaves Solana, and canonical WETH is what can arrive on Ethereum. The wrapper is not the coin that pays gas.

Send EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v from Phantom. Solscan is the source explorer, and there is no ERC-20 approval on that mint. Receive 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Ethereum, chain id 1. Etherscan is the check. Blocks are about 12 seconds. Native ETH is the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which this route does not deliver. WBTC is a different wrapper and is not native bitcoin.
description: Circle USDC leaves Solana and WETH arrives on Ethereum. WETH cannot pay gas. Hold ETH too. Check Solscan and Etherscan before you sign. Read the minimum.

sections.heading: Canonical WETH is one contract on chain id 1
sections.body: 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is the WETH people mean on mainnet. Base uses the predeploy 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Arbitrum uses 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Polygon uses 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. None of those balances are this hop. If the pool you must call is on an L2, landing in mainnet WETH is the wrong inventory and a second bridge.

sections.heading: The wrapper cannot pay the 12 second chain
sections.body: Ethereum gas is ETH. WETH sitting in the account does not broadcast a transaction. If you came here to refill fees, use the native ETH route. If a contract's function names WETH, this arrival matches and you still need a separate ETH float for the call. Arriving with only the wrapper recreates an empty-gas failure on a more expensive chain.

sections.heading: The Solana debit is a mint, not an allowance
sections.body: Phantom signs. MetaMask cannot see EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. There is nothing to revoke on Solscan in the ERC-20 sense. Native SOL has to remain for that signature. On the far side, an EVM wallet receives the WETH and must already hold ETH. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is why these are two tokens and not one balance walking across.

sections.heading: Refuse the route when the dollar should have stayed a dollar
sections.body: WETH tracks ether, not the Circle dollar you spent. A treasury that needed USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, Tether, or Maker DAI should not be on this page. A Solana pool that already trades the mint should not be abandoned for mainnet gas unless mainnet WETH is the asset. The minimum WETH is the floor. Quiet Etherscan is not a reason to send twice.

faqs.question: Can this WETH pay Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: No. WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is an ERC-20. Gas is native ETH on chain id 1, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Circle's mint left Solana. Hold ETH before you move the wrapper. Etherscan is the explorer, and about 12 second blocks are not a bridge schedule. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

faqs.question: Is this the same WETH used on Base?
faqs.answer: No. Base WETH is the predeploy 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on chain id 8453. This route delivers mainnet WETH only. Arbitrum and Polygon use other addresses too. If the app you are funding is not on chain id 1, this page is the wrong arrival. Check Etherscan before you assume the pool can see it.

faqs.question: Does Phantom show an approval for the USDC mint?
faqs.answer: No. EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v is an SPL mint. Solscan records the send, and there is no ERC-20 approval to revoke. Keep native SOL for the fee. The receiving wallet is an Ethereum account that needs its own ETH, because WETH will not pay the next mainnet transaction.

intro:
Swap USDT from Solana to USDC on Ethereum. Tether's SPL mint leaves Solana, and Circle's ERC-20 is what can arrive on Ethereum mainnet.

The mint is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Phantom signs it, Solscan shows it, and Solana will not ask for an ERC-20 approval. Circle on Ethereum is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, chain id 1. Etherscan is the arrival explorer. Blocks are about 12 seconds. That USDC is six decimals. It is not Tether, not DAI, and not the fee coin. ETH at 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE pays gas after it lands.
description: Tether USDT leaves Solana and Circle USDC arrives on Ethereum. Pay SOL, then hold ETH. Check Solscan and Etherscan before you sign the quote. Read the minimum.

sections.heading: Mainnet Circle is not mainnet Tether
sections.body: If the invoice says USDT, the contract is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and this route is wrong. That Tether contract has its own allowance behavior. Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is a third issuer. You are buying Circle specifically. Etherscan has to show 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. A USDC balance on Base or Arbitrum is a different chain even when the ticker matches.

sections.heading: Six decimals on the way in, an SPL mint on the way out
sections.body: Do not copy a raw amount from a Solana token account into an Ethereum unit field and assume the zeros line up. Circle on mainnet is six decimals. The bridge quote is the translation, not a notepad conversion. Phantom does not produce an allowance you must revoke. The first Ethereum transaction that spends the new USDC will be an approval or a transfer, and both want ETH on chain id 1.

sections.heading: SOL for the source, ETH for everything after
sections.body: An empty SOL balance stops the mint from leaving. An empty ETH balance stops the USDC from moving once Etherscan shows it. MetaMask cannot hold Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Phantom cannot hold the mainnet USDC. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is the side you are funding. About 12 seconds is a block interval, not the gap you should budget between the two explorers.

sections.heading: A Solana issuer swap is enough when mainnet was optional
sections.body: Tether and Circle both trade on Solana. If nobody named the Ethereum USDC contract, you are paying mainnet gas for a dollar you could have kept as an SPL mint. Bridge when 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 is the address on the instruction. Take the minimum as the floor. A second send while the first is still crossing spends the mint twice.

faqs.question: Will this Solana USDT arrive as Tether on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. The mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB leaves Solana and Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 is what can arrive on chain id 1. Tether's mainnet contract is different. Check Etherscan. If the receiver said USDT, this route is wrong. ETH is required to move the USDC. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

faqs.question: Is there an approval to clear on Solana?
faqs.answer: No. Tether there is an SPL mint, and Phantom does not use ERC-20 approvals. Solscan is the source explorer. Keep native SOL for the fee. On Ethereum, chain id 1, you may later approve the USDC, and that approval costs ETH. About 12 second blocks describe mainnet, not the bridge.

faqs.question: Which explorer proves the Circle credit?
faqs.answer: Etherscan, for 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on chain id 1. Solscan only proves the Solana mint left. Phantom will not display the Ethereum token. Make sure the receiving wallet is an EVM account with ETH for gas, or the USDC can arrive and still be unusable. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

intro:
Swap USDT from Solana to DAI on Ethereum. Tether's SPL mint leaves Solana, and Maker DAI is what can arrive on Ethereum. Two issuers, plus a change of account model.

Send Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB from Phantom. Solscan is the source explorer. There is no ERC-20 approval on that mint. DAI is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Ethereum, chain id 1. Etherscan is the check. Blocks are about 12 seconds. DAI is not Tether and not Circle. The gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is ETH, which DAI cannot replace.
description: Tether USDT leaves Solana and Maker DAI arrives on Ethereum. DAI is not Tether. Pay SOL, then ETH. Check Solscan and Etherscan before you sign. Read the floor.

sections.heading: A Tether balance does not become Circle on the way
sections.body: Some people treat every dollar ticker as interchangeable and discover the receiver wanted 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, Circle, or 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, Tether on mainnet. This page delivers Maker DAI only. If the collateral design of DAI is not what the desk accepts, stop. If they wanted Tether's mainnet contract, including its allowance rules, this is the wrong contract to wait for on Etherscan.

sections.heading: Mainnet gas is a separate purchase
sections.body: DAI cannot pay chain id 1. ETH can. About 12 seconds is how often Ethereum makes a block, not how long a bridge takes to show DAI. Phantom can finish while MetaMask still looks empty. Wait on the destination address instead of sending the mint again. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is the network that will hold 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F.

sections.heading: SOL stays behind as the source fee
sections.body: Native SOL pays Phantom's transaction. The USDT mint will not. MetaMask never held Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, so refreshing it tells you nothing about the debit. Solscan does. After arrival, the EVM wallet needs ETH before DAI can move. There is no Solana allowance to revoke, because the source was not an ERC-20 approval.

sections.heading: Pick this page only when DAI is the named asset
sections.body: USDT to USDC keeps you closer to a fiat-backed dollar from Circle. USDT to ETH buys gas. USDT to WETH buys the wrapper. USDT to DAI is for someone who wants Maker's token on mainnet. Anyone else is taking an issuer change they did not price. The minimum DAI is the floor. A local Solana swap is the better tool when the mint never had to leave.

faqs.question: Is the arrival Tether or Maker DAI?
faqs.answer: Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Ethereum, chain id 1. Tether's mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB is what leaves Solana. Circle's mainnet USDC is a different contract. Check Etherscan. If the receiver does not accept DAI, this route is wrong, and DAI will not pay gas. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

faqs.question: Do I need ETH before the DAI can move?
faqs.answer: Yes. Gas on chain id 1 is ETH, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, not DAI. Etherscan is the explorer, and blocks are about 12 seconds. That interval is not the bridge wait. Hold ETH in the receiving wallet or the new DAI sits still. SOL paid only the Solana side.

faqs.question: Can the same Phantom account show the DAI?
faqs.answer: No. DAI is an ERC-20. Phantom signed the SPL mint and cannot hold 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Use an Ethereum wallet and confirm the contract on Etherscan. There is no ERC-20 approval on the Solana send. Keep native SOL so that send can be broadcast. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

intro:
Swap USDT from Solana to ETH on Ethereum. Tether's SPL mint leaves Solana, and native ETH is what can arrive on Ethereum mainnet to pay gas.

The mint is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Phantom and Solscan handle it without an ERC-20 approval. The destination is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 1, which means ETH, not a token you import. Etherscan shows the native balance. This is not WETH, not WBTC, and not ETH on an L2. About 12 seconds is a mainnet block, not a delivery promise.
description: Tether USDT leaves Solana and native ETH arrives on Ethereum. That ETH pays mainnet gas. Check Solscan and Etherscan before you sign the quote. Read the floor.

sections.heading: The sentinel is mainnet ETH, not the wrapper
sections.body: Contracts that want 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 want WETH. This route will not satisfy them. WBTC,  which is not native bitcoin, is a different wrapper again and is not an output here. If the empty line in the wallet is the fee line, native ETH is the correct arrival. If the empty line is an ERC-20 field in a pool, you picked the fee coin for an inventory job. Read the app before you sell Tether.

sections.heading: L2 gas tanks are other chain ids
sections.body: Arbitrum One is 42161. Base is 8453. Both use ETH for fees and neither is credited by a mainnet arrival. Etherscan on chain id 1 is the only explorer that should move. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) covers the wallet change. Phantom cannot display the ETH, and a mainnet wallet cannot display the SPL mint that paid for it.

sections.heading: Do not spend the last SOL to buy ETH
sections.body: Native SOL is the source fee. Tether's mint does not pay it. A Phantom account at zero SOL cannot start the hop that was supposed to fund Ethereum. Leave enough SOL for the signature and for a retry if you reject the first preview. The preview is the moment to catch a bad minimum, not after Etherscan is involved.

sections.heading: Dollars were safer if gas was not the shortage
sections.body: USDT to USDC or USDT to DAI keeps you in a stablecoin on mainnet. USDT to WETH buys the wrapper. This page buys ETH, so the price of ether is now your problem until you spend it on fees or sell it. Compare the minimum ETH with the Tether you give up. Sign only if that floor still covers the mainnet actions you have queued.

faqs.question: Does this route deliver WETH or native ETH?
faqs.answer: Native ETH, quoted as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Ethereum, chain id 1. WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and is a different route. Tether's mint left Solana. Check the ETH line on Etherscan, not a token import of the sentinel. About 12 second blocks are not the bridge wait. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Will this ETH pay Base or Arbitrum fees?
faqs.answer: No. The arrival is mainnet, chain id 1, explorer Etherscan. Base is chain id 8453 and Arbitrum One is 42161. SOL paid the Phantom side. If the empty gas tank is on an L2, this page fills the wrong network. Do not resend the Solana mint while you are looking at the wrong chain id.

faqs.question: Is there an ERC-20 approval for the Solana USDT?
faqs.answer: No. Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB is an SPL mint. Phantom signs, Solscan records it, and there is no allowance to revoke. Keep native SOL for that fee. The ETH you receive is what pays later mainnet transactions, so the minimum should be large enough for that use. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

intro:
Swap USDT from Solana to WETH on Ethereum. Tether's SPL mint leaves Solana, and canonical WETH is what can arrive on Ethereum. You get the wrapper, not the gas coin.

Spend Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB in Phantom. Solscan shows the mint, and there is no ERC-20 approval. Receive 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1. Etherscan is the explorer. Blocks are about 12 seconds. Native ETH remains 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which you must hold separately. This is not Base WETH, not Arbitrum WETH, and not WBTC.
description: Tether USDT leaves Solana and WETH arrives on Ethereum. WETH is not gas. Hold ETH on mainnet. Check Solscan and Etherscan before you sign. Read the minimum.

sections.heading: Mainnet WETH still needs an ETH float beside it
sections.body: The pool that accepts 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 will not broadcast your deposit for free. Chain id 1 charges ETH. If the shortage you felt was gas, the native ETH route is the one that matches, and this page is wrong. If the shortage was the wrapper, arrive here and bring ETH anyway. WBTC is not a substitute, and WBTC is not native bitcoin.

sections.heading: Other chains reuse the name and not the contract
sections.body: Base's predeploy is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Arbitrum's WETH is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. A screenshot of either address does not credit Ethereum. Etherscan on chain id 1, with about 12 second blocks, is the only view that counts for this quote. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is that network. An L2 pool cannot see mainnet WETH, so bridging here to trade there is a detour.

sections.heading: Tether on Solana is a mint without an allowance
sections.body: Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB does not produce an ERC-20 approval in Phantom. Native SOL pays the signature. MetaMask cannot show the debit. After the hop, the EVM wallet may approve WETH, and that approval is a new Ethereum transaction. Tether's famous set-allowance-to-zero behavior belongs to mainnet USDT, not to this WETH and not to the SPL mint.

sections.heading: Stay in a stablecoin if ether exposure was not the request
sections.body: USDT to USDC or USDT to DAI keeps a dollar claim on mainnet. This route sells that claim for WETH. Use it when a mainnet contract named the canonical wrapper. Otherwise you are taking price risk and a bridge wait for the wrong inventory. The minimum WETH is the floor. Do not send a second mint transfer because Etherscan has not caught up with Solscan.

faqs.question: Does Solana USDT become WETH that can pay gas?
faqs.answer: No. WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 cannot pay gas. ETH, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, pays it on chain id 1. Tether's mint left Solana. Check Etherscan and hold ETH before you move the wrapper. About 12 second blocks are a mainnet fact, not a bridge clock. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

faqs.question: Is this WETH the Base predeploy?
faqs.answer: No. Base uses 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on chain id 8453. This route delivers Ethereum WETH only. If your contract is on Base or Arbitrum, you are on the wrong page. Etherscan must show 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 or the pool on mainnet cannot spend it. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

faqs.question: What signs the Solana half?
faqs.answer: Phantom or Solflare, against the mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Solscan is the explorer. There is no ERC-20 approval to revoke. Keep native SOL for the fee. The WETH arrives in an Ethereum wallet, which MetaMask can hold and Phantom cannot. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

intro:
Swap SOL from Solana to USDC on Ethereum. SOL leaves Solana, and Circle's ERC-20 is what can arrive on Ethereum mainnet.

The quote identifies SOL with the wrapped mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. Solscan shows it. Phantom signs it. Native SOL still pays the fee, so you cannot empty the wallet. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana. Circle on Ethereum is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, chain id 1, six decimals, checked on Etherscan. Blocks are about 12 seconds. ETH, not USDC, pays gas after arrival.
description: SOL leaves Solana and Circle USDC arrives on Ethereum. Keep SOL for the fee, then hold ETH. Check Solscan and Etherscan before you sign. Read the minimum.

sections.heading: Selling SOL can strand the signature that sells it
sections.body: The wrapped mint is how the route names SOL. The fee payer is native SOL in the same wallet. If the quote consumes every SOL, Phantom cannot pay for the transaction. Decide the fee remainder first. This is the mirror of selling all AVAX or all ETH on an EVM chain, with the extra detail that So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is not the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE.

sections.heading: Circle on mainnet is not Tether and not DAI
sections.body: Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and often wants an allowance reset to zero. Maker DAI is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. This route delivers neither. If the Ethereum instruction names those contracts, you are on the wrong page. Etherscan must show 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. USDC on Base or Solana is a different object even under the Circle name.

sections.heading: The receiving wallet needs ETH the USDC will not supply
sections.body: Chain id 1 charges ETH. A fresh address that receives USDC and nothing else cannot approve or transfer. Fund a little ETH first, or buy it with a different route. Phantom will not display the Ethereum token. MetaMask will not display So111. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the handoff. About 12 seconds describes a mainnet block, not the time between the two explorers.

sections.heading: A Jupiter-style swap is enough when you are not leaving
sections.body: SOL to Circle already exists on Solana as the mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Use that when the dollar can stay an SPL token. Cross to Ethereum only when someone named the mainnet contract. The minimum USDC is the floor. Do not resend because Etherscan is late. A second signature spends more SOL.

faqs.question: Should I swap all of my SOL for Ethereum USDC?
faqs.answer: No. Native SOL pays the Solana fee even though the quote names So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. An empty SOL balance cannot sign. Leave a remainder, then let Circle USDC arrive at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Check Solscan for the debit and Etherscan for the credit. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

faqs.question: Does this USDC pay Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is ETH on chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan. USDC is six-decimal Circle and cannot pay fees. Hold ETH in the receiving wallet. Phantom signed the SOL side and will not show the ERC-20. There is no ERC-20 approval on the Solana mint.

faqs.question: What if the receiver asked for Tether?
faqs.answer: Then this route is wrong. Tether on Ethereum is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, and Maker DAI is another contract. Circle will not satisfy either instruction. Switch routes before you sell SOL. The minimum on the quote only helps after the destination token is the one that was requested.

intro:
Swap SOL from Solana to USDT on Ethereum. SOL leaves Solana, and Tether's ERC-20 is what can arrive on Ethereum mainnet.

The route names SOL as So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, the wrapped mint. Phantom signs, Solscan records it, and native SOL pays the fee. There is no ERC-20 approval on that side. Tether on Ethereum is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, chain id 1, six decimals. Etherscan is the check. Blocks are about 12 seconds. That contract often wants an allowance set back to zero before a new approval. ETH pays gas. USDT does not.
description: SOL leaves Solana and Tether USDT arrives on Ethereum. Keep SOL for the fee, then ETH. Check Solscan and Etherscan before you sign the quote. Read the minimum.

sections.heading: Mainnet Tether adds an allowance ritual
sections.body: After USDT shows on Etherscan, the first spend can fail if an old allowance is not zero. 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is known for that. Reset to zero, then approve again, and pay ETH both times. None of this exists on the Solana side. Phantom will not show an allowance for So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. If you needed Circle instead, the contract is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 and this page is wrong.

sections.heading: Do not empty the SOL that has to sign
sections.body: Wrapped mint in the quote, native SOL in the fee payer. Selling the entire balance is how the preview never becomes a signature. Leave a remainder for the attempt and for a rejection if the minimum looks poor. MetaMask cannot hold the mint, so it cannot tell you whether the debit happened. Solscan can.

sections.heading: ETH has to be in the receiving account already
sections.body: USDT will not pay chain id 1. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is that ETH. A brand new mainnet address can receive Tether and still be unable to move it, including the allowance reset. About 12 second blocks describe Ethereum, not the bridge. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is the arrival. Base and Arbitrum USDT contracts are different addresses on different chain ids.

sections.heading: Keep SOL on Solana when the dollar can stay there
sections.body: Tether's Solana mint is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. A local swap reaches it without mainnet gas or the allowance quirk. Cross only when the creditor named the Ethereum contract. The minimum USDT is the floor. A quiet Etherscan page is a reason to wait on that address, not a reason to sell more SOL.

faqs.question: Why might spending the new USDT fail at approval?
faqs.answer: Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Ethereum often requires the allowance to return to zero first. That is an ERC-20 quirk on chain id 1, paid in ETH. It is not how Solana works. SOL left as the wrapped mint, checked on Solscan. Check the allowance on Etherscan before you raise it again.

faqs.question: Can I use every SOL in the wallet?
faqs.answer: No. Native SOL pays the fee even though the quote says So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. Leave a remainder or Phantom cannot sign. There is no ERC-20 approval on that mint. The USDT arrives on Ethereum and still needs ETH, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, before it can move. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Is this Circle USDC on mainnet?
faqs.answer: No. The arrival is Tether, not 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 and not Maker DAI. If the receiver said Circle, this route is wrong. Etherscan on chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, is the check. Those blocks do not schedule the bridge. Hold ETH so the USDT is not stuck.

intro:
Swap SOL from Solana to DAI on Ethereum. SOL leaves Solana, and Maker DAI is what can arrive on Ethereum. You are selling a gas coin for Maker's dollar.

SOL is quoted as So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. Phantom signs the wrapped mint, Solscan shows it, and native SOL pays the fee. There is no ERC-20 approval. DAI is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on chain id 1. Etherscan is the explorer. Blocks are about 12 seconds. DAI is not Circle and not Tether. ETH at 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE pays every later move.
description: SOL leaves Solana and Maker DAI arrives on Ethereum. DAI is not a fee coin. Keep SOL, then ETH. Check Solscan and Etherscan before you sign. Read the minimum.

sections.heading: Maker's dollar is a deliberate choice
sections.body: DAI is crypto-collateralized inside Maker's system. Circle on mainnet is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, with its allowance reset behavior. If a policy names either of those, this route is the wrong arrival even though all three can trade near a dollar. Etherscan has to show the Maker contract. A DAI balance on another chain is not this credit.

sections.heading: The SOL fee is paid before Ethereum ever sees you
sections.body: Empty the native SOL and the wrapped mint never leaves. So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 in the quote does not remove the need for a fee payer. MetaMask will stay dark during that debit. Solscan is the source of truth. Only later does an EVM wallet matter, and it needs ETH or the DAI cannot be transferred, sold, or deposited.

sections.heading: Twelve second blocks describe the destination chain only
sections.body: They do not describe the bridge, and they do not describe Solana. Refreshing Etherscan every block and then signing again is how people double-spend the mint. Wait for 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on the destination address. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the reason the two explorers update on different clocks. This page will not invent the gap.

sections.heading: Skip mainnet if DAI was not the asset you will hold
sections.body: SOL to ETH buys gas. SOL to WETH buys the canonical wrapper. SOL to USDC or USDT buys a different issuer. SOL to DAI is right when Maker's token is what the contract calls. Otherwise you have sold a fee coin on Solana for a stablecoin you must bridge again. Read the minimum DAI and refuse a floor you would not keep.

faqs.question: Is DAI from SOL the same as Circle USDC?
faqs.answer: No. Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is the arrival on Ethereum, chain id 1. Circle and Tether are different contracts. SOL left as the wrapped mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. Check Etherscan. If the desk rejects DAI, this route is wrong, and DAI cannot pay gas. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

faqs.question: What do I leave in Phantom?
faqs.answer: Native SOL for the fee. The quote can spend the wrapped mint, but the signature still needs SOL. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solscan for that mint. After the hop, the Ethereum wallet needs ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, before DAI can move. Phantom will not display the ERC-20.

faqs.question: Do Ethereum's 12 second blocks time this bridge?
faqs.answer: No. They describe chain id 1 only. The bridge between Solscan and Etherscan has its own wait, and this page does not schedule it. Do not send a second SOL transfer because DAI is not visible yet. Confirm 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on the destination address first. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

intro:
Swap SOL from Solana to ETH on Ethereum. SOL leaves Solana, and native ETH is what can arrive on Ethereum mainnet. You exchange one fee coin for another, across two account models.

The quote names So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, the wrapped SOL mint. Phantom signs it, Solscan shows it, and native SOL pays the source fee. There is no ERC-20 approval. ETH arrives as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 1. Etherscan shows a native balance, not a token import. This is not WETH, not L2 ETH, and not WBTC. About 12 seconds is a mainnet block, not the bridge.
description: SOL leaves Solana and native ETH arrives on Ethereum. Both are gas coins on different systems. Check Solscan and Etherscan before you sign. Read the minimum.

sections.heading: Wrapped SOL in the quote, native SOL in the fee payer
sections.body: So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is how SPL programs name SOL. It is not the EVM sentinel, and it is not something MetaMask can hold. If you sell every native SOL, Phantom cannot pay for the sale. Leave a remainder. The ETH you hope to receive cannot be spent until it exists on chain id 1, so it cannot pay the Solana transaction that creates it.

sections.heading: Mainnet ETH is not the ETH on Base or Arbitrum
sections.body: Chain id 1, Etherscan, about 12 second blocks. Base is 8453. Arbitrum One is 42161. A request for L2 gas is a different route. WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is also different: it is the wrapper, and this page does not deliver it. WBTC is not native bitcoin and is not an output here. If the contract wants the wrapper, change pages before you sell SOL.

sections.heading: Do not import the sentinel as a token
sections.body: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means native ETH on this destination. The balance is the ETH row. An importer that treats the sentinel as an ERC-20 will show nonsense. Phantom will not show that row either. Switch your attention to an Ethereum wallet after Solscan confirms the debit. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is the arrival network and only that network.

sections.heading: Buy ETH only when mainnet fees are the shortage
sections.body: If you needed Circle, Tether, or DAI, a dollar route avoids turning SOL into a volatile coin you must sell again. If you needed WETH for a pool, the wrapper route matches the ABI. If you needed more SOL, do not leave Solana. The minimum ETH is the floor. Silence on Etherscan is not permission to sign a second time.

faqs.question: Why do SOL and ETH use different address styles?
faqs.answer: SOL on this quote is the wrapped mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, checked on Solscan, held in Phantom. ETH is the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Ethereum, chain id 1, checked on Etherscan. There is no ERC-20 approval on the Solana side. Native SOL still pays the source fee. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

faqs.question: Can the ETH I receive pay fees on an L2?
faqs.answer: No. It arrives on mainnet. Base is chain id 8453 and Arbitrum One is 42161. About 12 second blocks describe chain id 1 only, not those networks and not the bridge. If the gas you lack is on an L2, this route is the wrong destination. WETH is a separate contract as well.

faqs.question: What if the pool wants WETH instead of ETH?
faqs.answer: Use the WETH route. Native ETH will not match 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 until you wrap, and wrapping needs ETH for gas. If the ABI names the wrapper, this page stops short. Leave enough SOL in Phantom that the source transaction can still be signed. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

intro:
Swap SOL from Solana to WETH on Ethereum. SOL leaves Solana, and canonical WETH is what can arrive on Ethereum. The wrapper cannot pay mainnet gas.

You spend the wrapped SOL mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, signed in Phantom and shown on Solscan, while native SOL pays the fee. There is no ERC-20 approval. You receive 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1. Etherscan is the check. Blocks are about 12 seconds. Native ETH is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and is not included. WBTC is not this token and is not native bitcoin.
description: SOL leaves Solana and WETH arrives on Ethereum. The wrapper cannot pay gas. Keep SOL, then ETH. Check Solscan and Etherscan before you sign. Read the minimum.

sections.heading: Canonical WETH is inventory for mainnet contracts
sections.body: 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is the address pools on chain id 1 expect. It does not pay the transaction that deposits it. Bring ETH, or use the native ETH route if fees were the only gap. Base's predeploy and Arbitrum's WETH are other contracts on other chain ids. Bridging SOL into mainnet WETH does not fill an L2 pool. If that L2 is where you trade, this page is the wrong stop.

sections.heading: Leave native SOL or the mint never moves
sections.body: The quote's mint and the fee payer are related and not identical. Draining SOL to buy WETH fails in Phantom before Etherscan is involved. There is no allowance on Solscan to clean up afterward. MetaMask cannot show So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, so do not use it as the progress bar. Solscan is the debit. Etherscan is the credit.

sections.heading: About 12 seconds is not a promise about WETH
sections.body: That is Ethereum's block interval. The bridge adds its own wait, and this page will not name it. Refreshing every block and signing again spends more SOL. Wait until the destination address holds 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) explains the lock on one side and the release on the other.

sections.heading: Choose a dollar or the fee coin when WETH is not in the ABI
sections.body: Circle, Tether, and Maker DAI are the stable arrivals. Native ETH is the fee arrival. WETH is for a contract that names the wrapper. Selling SOL into WETH and then unwrapping wastes a step you could have skipped. Read the minimum WETH. If the floor is less ether than you will accept for the SOL, do not sign.

faqs.question: Can the WETH from SOL pay Ethereum fees?
faqs.answer: No. 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is an ERC-20. Gas is native ETH on chain id 1. SOL left as the wrapped mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112.
