Hold ETH before you move WETH. Etherscan is the explorer. About 12 second blocks do not time the bridge. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

faqs.question: Do I approve SOL in Phantom?
faqs.answer: No. There is no ERC-20 approval for So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. Solscan shows the send. Native SOL still has to remain for the fee, or the wallet cannot sign. The WETH arrives in an Ethereum wallet, not in Phantom. MetaMask can hold it only after you switch to chain id 1.

faqs.question: Is this WETH usable on Base without another hop?
faqs.answer: No. Base WETH is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on chain id 8453. This route credits Ethereum only. If the pool is on Base or Arbitrum, mainnet WETH is the wrong inventory. Check Etherscan, and do not treat a shared nickname as a shared balance. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

intro:
Swap USDC from Solana to USDT on BNB Chain. Circle's SPL mint leaves Solana, and Binance-pegged USDT is what can arrive on BNB Chain. The decimals change with the chain.

You send EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v from Phantom. Solscan shows the mint, and there is no ERC-20 approval. The arrival is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BNB Chain, chain id 56. BscScan is the explorer. Blocks are about 3 seconds. That pegged USDT uses 18 decimals, not the 6 decimals of Ethereum's Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. BNB pays gas. The USDT does not.
description: Circle USDC leaves Solana and pegged USDT arrives on BNB Chain. It uses 18 decimals. Pay SOL, then BNB. Check Solscan and BscScan before you sign now.

sections.heading: Eighteen decimals will make the balance look huge
sections.body: A unit copied from Solana's six-decimal USDC into this 18-decimal peg will be off by twelve zeros. Trust the quote, not a hand conversion. 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 is BSC-USD, a pegged Tether, not the Ethereum contract and not its allowance-reset behavior. If a form was written for mainnet USDT, this arrival is the wrong token even though the ticker matches. BscScan on chain id 56 is the proof.

sections.heading: BNB is the fee, and three second blocks are not the bridge
sections.body: Chain id 56 charges BNB. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means that native gas, not the USDT contract. About 3 seconds is how often BNB Chain produces a block. It does not say when Solscan's debit becomes a BscScan credit. Do not resend the mint because the second explorer is quiet. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is the network you are entering, and only that network.

sections.heading: Phantom out, an EVM wallet in
sections.body: MetaMask cannot hold the Circle mint. Phantom cannot hold the pegged USDT. Native SOL has to remain so the source can sign. Native BNB has to be present so the USDT can move after it lands. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana to revoke. The first BNB Chain approval, if you need one, is a new transaction paid in BNB.

sections.heading: Stay on Solana if nobody named the peg
sections.body: Circle and Tether both exist as SPL mints. A local swap never touches 18-decimal BSC-USD or chain id 56. Use this page when the receiver wrote 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. The minimum is the floor. A pegged dollar can still slip, so refuse a quote that gives you fewer units than you will accept.

faqs.question: Is BNB Chain USDT the same contract as Ethereum USDT?
faqs.answer: No. This route delivers 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955, an 18-decimal peg on chain id 56. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and uses 6 decimals. Circle's mint left Solana. Check BscScan, not Etherscan. BNB pays gas, and about 3 second blocks are not the bridge wait. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

faqs.question: Does the pegged USDT pay BNB Chain fees?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is native BNB, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on chain id 56. Hold BNB before you move the USDT. Phantom signed the SPL side and will not show this token. There is no ERC-20 approval on EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Keep SOL for that signature. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

faqs.question: When is this USDT route the wrong one?
faqs.answer: When the receiver wanted Ethereum's 6-decimal Tether, Circle on BNB Chain, or native BNB for gas. The peg is a different contract. It is also wrong if the dollars could have stayed on Solana as an SPL mint. Read the minimum on the quote and do not sign a floor you would not hold.

intro:
Swap USDC from Solana to ETH on BNB Chain. Circle's SPL mint leaves Solana, and Binance-Peg Ethereum Token is what can arrive. That token is not native ETH and it does not pay gas.

You spend EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v in Phantom, with Solscan as the explorer and no ERC-20 approval. The arrival contract is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BNB Chain, chain id 56. BscScan is the check. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Gas is BNB, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, not this peg. Ethereum mainnet ETH is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, on Etherscan, and this route does not deliver it.
description: Circle USDC leaves Solana and pegged ETH arrives on BNB Chain. That token is not gas. Pay SOL, then BNB. Check Solscan and BscScan before you sign now.

sections.heading: The ticker ETH here is a pegged ERC-20
sections.body: 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is Binance-Peg Ethereum Token. It is not WETH on Ethereum, not the canonical mainnet wrapper 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and not WBTC, which is not native bitcoin. It cannot pay a BNB Chain fee. If you needed gas, the BNB route is the one that matches. If you needed ether you can spend on chain id 1, this peg is the wrong asset on the wrong chain.

sections.heading: Three second blocks belong to BNB Chain alone
sections.body: They do not describe Solana and they do not describe the bridge. Phantom can show the USDC gone while BscScan still shows nothing at the peg address. Wait for 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on the destination. Sending again spends another mint. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is chain id 56. A wallet left on Ethereum will hide the peg entirely.

sections.heading: SOL out, BNB in, and the peg is neither
sections.body: Keep native SOL so Phantom can sign. Keep native BNB so you can transfer the pegged token afterward. The Circle mint does not pay Solana, and the peg does not pay chain id 56. There is no ERC-20 allowance on the Solana side to revoke. MetaMask can hold the peg only after you switch to BNB Chain. It cannot hold EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v at all.

sections.heading: Use this page only when the peg is what the contract named
sections.body: Many people type ETH and mean mainnet gas or WETH. This quote means a BEP-20 claim. If the app on BNB Chain calls the peg, you are in the right place and you still need BNB. If the app calls native BNB, or USDT, or real ETH on Ethereum, leave. The minimum amount of the peg is the floor. Do not treat a familiar ticker as a familiar contract.

faqs.question: Is ETH on BNB Chain the same as ETH on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. The arrival is Binance-Peg Ethereum Token at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on chain id 56. Native ETH on Ethereum is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan. This peg does not pay gas. BNB does. Circle's mint left Solana. Check BscScan, not Etherscan. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

faqs.question: Can this pegged ETH pay BNB Chain fees?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is native BNB, quoted as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. The peg is an ERC-20. Hold BNB before you move it. About 3 second blocks describe chain id 56, not the bridge. Phantom will not display the peg. There is no ERC-20 approval on the Solana USDC mint.

faqs.question: When should I avoid this ETH route?
faqs.answer: When you needed native ETH on Ethereum, WETH on mainnet, or BNB for fees. The peg will not satisfy those jobs. It is also wrong if you needed a dollar token such as pegged USDT. Read the minimum before you sell Circle's mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, and confirm the contract on BscScan.

intro:
Swap USDC from Solana to BNB on BNB Chain. Circle's SPL mint leaves Solana, and native BNB is what can arrive to pay gas on chain id 56.

You send EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Phantom signs, Solscan records it, and there is no ERC-20 approval. BNB arrives as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the native gas sentinel, on BNB Chain. BscScan shows a native balance, not a token import of that sentinel. Blocks are about 3 seconds. This is not the pegged ETH token at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, and it is not Ethereum mainnet ETH.
description: Circle USDC leaves Solana and native BNB arrives on BNB Chain. BNB pays gas on chain id 56. Check Solscan and BscScan before you sign the quote. Read it.

sections.heading: You are buying the fee coin, not a pegged ether
sections.body: People confuse BNB with the token labeled ETH on BscScan. The ETH label is the peg 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, an ERC-20 that cannot pay fees. This route delivers native BNB. Do not import the sentinel as a token. Read the BNB row after you switch the wallet to chain id 56. If a contract wants the pegged ether, this page is the wrong arrival.

sections.heading: About 3 seconds is a block, not a delivery
sections.body: BNB Chain blocks are quick compared with Ethereum's about 12 second blocks on chain id 1. The bridge still sits between Solscan and BscScan. A fast chain does not make the hop instant, and this page will not name a finish time. Wait for native BNB on the destination address. A second signature spends more Circle mint. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the sequence, including the wallet change.

sections.heading: Keep SOL even though you are trying to obtain BNB
sections.body: The BNB you might receive cannot pay the Solana transaction that requests it. Native SOL has to be in Phantom first. MetaMask cannot see the mint leaving. After arrival, the EVM wallet on chain id 56 should show BNB without an approval. If it asks you to approve 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, you are on the wrong screen.

sections.heading: A dollar peg is the better arrival when gas is not the gap
sections.body: Pegged USDT and pegged USDC exist on BNB Chain if you need spending dollars rather than fee BNB. Buying BNB means taking BNB's price for the life of the quote. Do that when you have transactions to send on chain id 56. Otherwise stay in Circle, either on Solana or as a pegged dollar. The minimum BNB is the floor you either accept or reject.

faqs.question: Is the BNB from this route the pegged ETH token?
faqs.answer: No. Native BNB arrives, quoted as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 56. The pegged ETH token is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 and cannot pay gas. Circle's mint left Solana. Check the BNB line on BscScan. About 3 second blocks are not a bridge schedule. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

faqs.question: Will this BNB pay Ethereum mainnet fees?
faqs.answer: No. It arrives on BNB Chain. Ethereum is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan, and its fee coin is ETH. Phantom cannot hold the BNB, and MetaMask must be on chain id 56 to see it. SOL paid the source side. There is no ERC-20 approval on the Solana mint.

faqs.question: What if I needed a dollar on BNB Chain instead?
faqs.answer: Use a USDT or USDC route. Those are pegged ERC-20s, not native BNB. This page is wrong when the next step is a stablecoin transfer rather than a fee. Keep native SOL so Phantom can sign EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, and read the minimum BNB before you accept the price.

intro:
Swap USDT from Solana to USDC on BNB Chain. Tether's SPL mint leaves Solana, and Binance-Peg USDC is what can arrive. The peg is 18 decimals, not Circle's 6-decimal mainnet token.

Send Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB from Phantom. Solscan is the explorer, and there is no ERC-20 approval. Receive 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BNB Chain, chain id 56. BscScan is the check. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Ethereum's Circle USDC is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on chain id 1 and is not this balance. BNB, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, pays gas.
description: Tether USDT leaves Solana and pegged USDC arrives on BNB Chain. It uses 18 decimals. Pay SOL, then BNB. Check Solscan and BscScan before you sign now.

sections.heading: Pegged USDC is not Ethereum's Circle contract
sections.body: Twelve extra decimal places change how a raw balance looks. 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d will not satisfy a mainnet function written for 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. It also will not satisfy Solana's Circle mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, which you are not receiving. If the app on BNB Chain still expects a different dollar, read the address on BscScan before you call the hop finished.

sections.heading: Tether in, Circle's peg out
sections.body: You are changing issuer as well as chain. Pegged USDT on BNB Chain is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. If that is the contract a counterparty named, this USDC arrival is the wrong page. Native BNB is the fee route. The pegged ETH token is a third page. Pick from the address, not from the habit of saying dollars.

sections.heading: SOL signs, BNB spends, three second blocks wait in between
sections.body: About 3 seconds describes chain id 56, not the bridge and not Ethereum's about 12 second blocks. Keep native SOL in Phantom. Keep BNB in the EVM wallet or the new USDC cannot move. There is no allowance to revoke on the SPL mint. MetaMask sees the peg only on chain id 56. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is that network. Do not resend while BscScan is still empty.

sections.heading: A local mint swap is enough when BNB Chain was optional
sections.body: Tether and Circle already meet on Solana. Crossing into an 18-decimal peg is justified when a BNB Chain contract named 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. Otherwise you are buying a decimal surprise and a second fee coin. The minimum USDC is the floor. A peg can slip. Refuse a number you would not deposit.

faqs.question: Is this the 6-decimal USDC from Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. The arrival is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, an 18-decimal peg on BNB Chain, chain id 56. Ethereum Circle is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on chain id 1. Tether's mint left Solana. Check BscScan. BNB pays gas. About 3 second blocks are not the bridge wait. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

faqs.question: Does pegged USDC pay the BNB Chain fee?
faqs.answer: No. Native BNB, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, pays it. Hold BNB before you transfer the peg. Phantom signed Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB and will not show the BEP-20. There is no ERC-20 approval on that mint. Keep SOL for the source signature. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: What if the BNB Chain app wants USDT?
faqs.answer: Then this route is wrong. Pegged USDT is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955, a different contract. USDC will not satisfy that address. Switch routes before you leave Solana. Read the minimum only after the destination contract matches the one in the app. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

intro:
Swap USDT from Solana to ETH on BNB Chain. Tether's SPL mint leaves Solana, and Binance-Peg Ethereum Token is what can arrive. You do not receive native ETH, and you do not receive BNB.

The mint is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Phantom and Solscan handle it with no ERC-20 approval. The peg is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on chain id 56. BscScan is the explorer. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Gas is BNB at 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Mainnet ETH is chain id 1, about 12 seconds, Etherscan, and WETH there is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. None of those are this peg.
description: Tether USDT leaves Solana and pegged ETH arrives on BNB Chain. The peg is not native ETH. Pay SOL, then BNB. Check Solscan and BscScan before you sign.

sections.heading: Pegged ether cannot fund a BNB transaction
sections.body: If the wallet error says you need gas, this route answers with an ERC-20 and leaves the error in place. Native BNB is the fix. If a BEP-20 contract names 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, this arrival matches and you still owe BNB for the call. WBTC is not involved, and WBTC is not native bitcoin. Do not tell someone you sent them ETH on Ethereum. You would be describing a different chain and a different asset.

sections.heading: Mainnet and this peg share a nickname only
sections.body: Chain id 1 uses Etherscan and about 12 second blocks. Chain id 56 uses BscScan and about 3 second blocks. The bridge is slower than both facts and is not given a time here. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the model: the mint locks or burns, and a different contract is released. Wait for the peg address. A second Phantom signature is a second sale of Tether.

sections.heading: Two fee coins bracket the peg
sections.body: SOL must remain in Phantom. BNB must sit in the EVM wallet before the peg can move. The Tether mint pays neither. There is no Solana allowance to clear. MetaMask shows the peg only after the network is BNB Chain. A wallet still on Ethereum mainnet will look empty and invite a duplicate send.

sections.heading: Choose BNB or a dollar when the peg was a mistaken ticker
sections.body: USDT to BNB buys gas. USDT to pegged USDC stays in a dollar. USDT to this ETH token buys a claim on ether that lives only as a BEP-20. Use it when that claim is what you will hold or deposit. The minimum is the floor. A thin quote is a reason to stop, not a reason to hope the peg trades back to the dollar you left.

faqs.question: Does Solana USDT become native ETH on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. The arrival is the peg at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BNB Chain, chain id 56. Native ETH is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, Etherscan. WETH there is a different contract. This peg cannot pay gas. BNB can. Check BscScan. Tether's mint left Solana. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

faqs.question: What pays fees on BNB Chain after the peg arrives?
faqs.answer: Native BNB, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. About 3 second blocks describe chain id 56, not the bridge. Hold BNB before you transfer 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Phantom will not show the peg. There is no ERC-20 approval on Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

faqs.question: Is this the right route for a gas top-up?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is BNB, and this page delivers pegged ETH. Use the BNB route if fees are the shortage. Use this page only when a contract names the peg. Keep native SOL so the Solana mint can leave, and read the minimum before you take ether price risk.

intro:
Swap USDT from Solana to BNB on BNB Chain. Tether's SPL mint leaves Solana, and native BNB is what can arrive to pay gas on chain id 56.

You send Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Phantom signs, Solscan shows the mint, and there is no ERC-20 approval. BNB is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on BNB Chain. BscScan shows the native row. Blocks are about 3 seconds. This is not pegged ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 and not pegged USDT at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. Ethereum's fee coin is a different chain.
description: Tether USDT leaves Solana and native BNB arrives on BNB Chain. BNB pays gas on chain id 56. Check Solscan and BscScan before you sign the quote. Read it.

sections.heading: Native BNB is the row you should read
sections.body: Do not import the sentinel as an ERC-20. After the wallet is on chain id 56, the BNB balance is the fee balance. The pegged token people call ETH cannot substitute, and a dollar peg cannot substitute. If your next click is a contract that wants 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, you bought the wrong asset. If your next click is any transaction at all, BNB is what it will burn.

sections.heading: A fast block time still is not the hop
sections.body: About 3 seconds is BNB Chain. About 12 seconds is Ethereum, chain id 1, Etherscan, and that chain is not the destination. The bridge has its own wait. This page will not turn either block interval into a promise. Watch the destination address on BscScan. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is the only network where this BNB can pay. A wallet left on Solana or Ethereum will not show it.

sections.heading: Tether cannot pay the Phantom signature
sections.body: Native SOL pays it. Spending the last SOL to chase BNB fails before BscScan matters. There is no ERC-20 approval on the mint to revoke later. MetaMask cannot display Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, so it is the wrong window for the debit. Phantom is the debit. An EVM wallet on chain id 56 is the credit.

sections.heading: Buy BNB when you have BNB Chain transactions waiting
sections.body: If you needed a dollar, stay with a pegged USDC or USDT route and avoid BNB's price. If you needed mainnet ETH, this is the wrong chain and the wrong ticker. The minimum BNB should cover the fees you came to buy, with room for more than one transaction. Sign only if that floor still makes the trip worthwhile.

faqs.question: Does this route deliver pegged USDT or native BNB?
faqs.answer: Native BNB, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 56. Pegged USDT is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 and is a different route. Tether's mint left Solana. Check the BNB row on BscScan. About 3 second blocks do not time the bridge. The pegged ETH token is not this arrival either.

faqs.question: Can I receive the BNB in Phantom?
faqs.answer: No. Phantom holds the SPL mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB and signs with SOL. BNB is an EVM gas coin on chain id 56. Use an EVM wallet and BscScan. There is no ERC-20 approval on the Solana side. Do not import the gas sentinel as a token contract.

faqs.question: Will this BNB pay fees on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan, fee coin ETH. This BNB pays BNB Chain only. If mainnet gas was the shortage, this page is the wrong destination. Keep SOL for the source fee, and judge the quote by the minimum BNB, not by a hoped-for wait.

description: SOL leaves Solana and pegged USDC arrives on BNB Chain. The peg uses 18 decimals. Keep SOL, then BNB. Check Solscan and BscScan before you sign it now.

sections.heading: Do not read this balance with six-decimal habits
sections.body: 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d uses 18 decimals. Circle on Ethereum, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, uses 6, on chain id 1, Etherscan, about 12 second blocks. The same nickname hides both. A withdrawal form or a spreadsheet that assumes six decimals will mis-state the peg by orders of magnitude. BscScan is the display that matches the contract. sections.heading: Selling SOL still requires SOL

MetaMask cannot show So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, so it cannot confirm the debit. After the hop, the pegged USDC cannot pay chain id 56. Bring BNB or the dollars sit still. sections.heading: About 3 seconds does not schedule BscScan
sections.body: That is the chain's block interval. The bridge is extra, and this page will not clock it. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) separates the source signature from the destination credit. Wait for the peg address. A second sale of SOL because the first looks missing is how balances disappear twice.

sections.heading: Stay in SOL or in a Solana mint when BNB Chain is not the venue
sections.body: Circle's SPL mint is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. If the dollar can live there, you avoid the 18-decimal peg and the BNB fee coin. Cross when a BNB Chain app named 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. Pegged USDT is a different address if the app said Tether. The minimum USDC is the floor.

faqs.question: Can I spend all my SOL on this swap?

The USDC that arrives still needs BNB, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, before it can move. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

Confirm whichever contract you do receive on BscScan, chain id 56, and do not assume a dollar ticker selects the address for you. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

description: SOL leaves Solana and pegged USDT arrives on BNB Chain. The peg uses 18 decimals, not 6. Keep SOL, then BNB. Check Solscan and BscScan before you sign.

sections.heading: BSC-USD is not the Tether contract traders know from mainnet
sections.body: Mainnet USDT uses 6 decimals and often demands an allowance reset to zero. 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 uses 18 decimals and is a peg on BNB Chain. Copying an amount or an approval habit from Etherscan will mislead you. About 12 second blocks and chain id 1 belong to that other Tether. If a counterparty pasted the Ethereum address, this route is the wrong delivery. BscScan has to show the peg.

sections.body: So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 names SOL for SPL programs. The fee payer is native SOL. Drain it and there is no signature. MetaMask will not help you watch the debit. Afterward the peg cannot pay chain id 56, so an EVM wallet with zero BNB is stuck holding dollars it cannot send. There is nothing on Solscan to revoke in the ERC-20 sense.

sections.heading: Three second blocks are the chain, not the bridge
sections.body: BNB Chain can confirm its own transactions quickly and still leave you waiting on the hop from Solana. This page does not publish that wait. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is where the peg lives. Refresh BscScan for the destination, not a timer. A second SOL transfer while the first is in flight spends inventory you may have needed for fees.

sections.heading: Pegged USDC, native BNB, and mainnet Tether are other jobs
sections.body: USDC on BNB Chain is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. BNB is the gas sentinel. Ethereum Tether is the 6-decimal contract. This page is only for someone who will hold or spend 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. The minimum is the floor. A local swap to Solana's Tether mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB is the smaller move when you are not leaving.

faqs.question: Why must I keep SOL if I am selling SOL?
faqs.answer: Native SOL pays the Phantom fee. The quote's mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 does not remove that need. There is no ERC-20 approval. Empty the fee balance and the send never broadcasts. On the other side, hold BNB, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, or the peg cannot move. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

faqs.question: Is pegged USDC an acceptable substitute here?
faqs.answer: Only if the receiver accepts 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. This route does not deliver it. If the app named the USDT peg, stay on this page. If it named USDC, switch. Confirm the contract on BscScan before you treat a dollar balance as the right dollar. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

intro:
Swap SOL from Solana to ETH on BNB Chain. SOL leaves Solana, and Binance-Peg Ethereum Token is what can arrive. That is a BEP-20, not native ETH, not WETH, and not gas.

You spend So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, the wrapped SOL mint, in Phantom. Solscan shows it. Native SOL pays the fee. There is no ERC-20 approval. The peg is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on chain id 56. BscScan is the explorer. Blocks are about 3 seconds. BNB is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and is what pays fees. Mainnet WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1. WBTC is not this peg and is not native bitcoin.
description: SOL leaves Solana and pegged ETH arrives on BNB Chain. The peg is not native ETH or WETH. Keep SOL, then BNB. Check Solscan and BscScan before you sign.

sections.heading: A familiar ticker hides a BEP-20 claim
sections.body: 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 cannot pay chain id 56 and cannot pay Ethereum. If you needed mainnet ether, chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, Etherscan, this page sent you to the wrong network. If you needed canonical WETH, the address is different. If you needed BNB for gas, the sentinel route is the one that matches. This peg is right only when a BNB Chain contract names it.

sections.heading: The SOL you sell is not the SOL that pays
sections.body: Drain native SOL and Phantom stops. The wrapped mint in the quote does not waive the fee. MetaMask cannot confirm So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 left. Solscan can. Later, an EVM wallet on chain id 56 needs BNB before the peg can be deposited. Arriving in pegged ETH with an empty BNB line recreates the stuck-wallet problem on the far side.

sections.heading: Do not time the hop with a 3 second block
sections.body: That interval is BNB Chain's, not the bridge's. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the picture: one asset is committed on Solana, another contract is released on BNB Chain. Wait for the peg on the destination address. Signing twice because BscScan looks empty spends SOL you may not recover if both transfers complete.

sections.heading: Dollars or BNB are calmer when ether was not the point
sections.body: Pegged USDT and pegged USDC keep you in a dollar. Native BNB buys fees. This route buys a pegged ether claim and its price. Take it when you will hold that claim. Read the minimum. A quote that turns a large SOL balance into a thin peg is a reason to walk away, not a reason to trust the ticker ETH.

faqs.question: Is ETH on BNB Chain from SOL the same as mainnet ETH?
faqs.answer: No. You receive the peg 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on chain id 56. Mainnet ETH is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, Etherscan. WETH there is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. This peg cannot pay gas. BNB can. SOL left as the wrapped mint. Check BscScan. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

faqs.question: What has to stay in the Solana wallet?
faqs.answer: Native SOL, so Phantom can pay the fee. The quote uses So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 and does not use an ERC-20 approval. Solscan shows the debit. After arrival, the EVM wallet needs BNB, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, or the peg cannot be transferred on chain id 56. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

faqs.question: Should I use this route to refill gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on BNB Chain is BNB, and this page delivers pegged ETH. Use the BNB route for fees. Use this page when a contract names 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. About 3 second blocks are not a delivery promise. Read the minimum before you sell SOL. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

intro:
Swap SOL from Solana to BNB on BNB Chain. SOL leaves Solana, and native BNB is what can arrive. You trade one fee coin for the fee coin on chain id 56.

SOL is So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 in the quote, the wrapped mint. Phantom signs, Solscan shows it, native SOL pays the source fee, and there is no ERC-20 approval. BNB is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on BNB Chain. BscScan shows the native balance. Blocks are about 3 seconds. This is not pegged ETH and not a dollar peg. It is not ETH on Ethereum, chain id 1.
description: SOL leaves Solana and native BNB arrives on BNB Chain. Both are gas coins on different chains. Check Solscan and BscScan before you sign the quote now.

sections.heading: Two gas coins, two address styles
sections.body: So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 means nothing in an Ethereum token box. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means nothing in Phantom. Do not paste either into the other's form. Do not import the sentinel as a BEP-20. Read the BNB row on chain id 56. If you empty native SOL, the transaction that was supposed to buy BNB never starts.

sections.heading: Pegged ETH is the decoy
sections.body: 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 wears the ticker ETH and cannot pay fees. People buy it when they meant BNB. This page is the gas route. It is the wrong page when a contract wants that peg, pegged USDT, or pegged USDC. WBTC is not an output, and WBTC is not native bitcoin. BscScan is how you prove you received BNB rather than a token that merely sounds like a major asset.

sections.heading: Block speed is not hop speed
sections.body: About 3 seconds is BNB Chain. About 12 seconds is Ethereum on Etherscan, which you are not funding. The bridge is a third interval, and this page will not guess it. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is the arrival. Wait for native BNB on the destination. Phantom going to zero SOL is the debit. It is not, by itself, the credit.

sections.heading: Cross only when chain id 56 is where you will transact
sections.body: If you need SOL for Solana fees, selling it for BNB is the opposite of the job. If you need mainnet ETH, this BNB cannot pay it. If you need a dollar, a peg route keeps price risk smaller. The minimum BNB should be enough for the transactions you already know you will send. Refuse a floor that leaves you short of gas on the chain you just paid to enter.

faqs.question: Are the SOL mint and the BNB sentinel the same idea?
faqs.answer: No. SOL is So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, an SPL mint on Solscan, held in Phantom, with no ERC-20 approval. BNB is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 56, shown on BscScan as native gas. Native SOL still pays the source fee. The two balances cannot pay each other's chains. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

faqs.question: Does this BNB work on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan, fee coin ETH. This arrival pays BNB Chain only. About 3 second blocks describe chain id 56, not the bridge and not mainnet. If you needed mainnet gas, this route is the wrong destination.

faqs.question: What if I needed the token labeled ETH on BscScan?
faqs.answer: Use the pegged ETH route. That contract is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, and native BNB will not satisfy it. This page is for gas. Leave enough SOL in Phantom to sign, and check the BNB row rather than a token list after you switch to chain id 56.

intro:
Swap USDC from Solana to USDT on Polygon. Circle's SPL mint leaves Solana, and Tether on Polygon is what can arrive. POL, not USDT, pays the next fee.

Send EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v from Phantom. Solscan shows the mint, and there is no ERC-20 approval. Tether on Polygon is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F, chain id 137. Polygonscan is the explorer. Gas is POL, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. This is not Circle's Polygon USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, and it is not Ethereum's Tether on chain id 1.
description: Circle USDC leaves Solana and Tether USDT arrives on Polygon. POL pays gas, not USDT. Check Solscan and Polygonscan before you sign the quote. Read it.

sections.heading: Tether on Polygon is a specific PoS contract
sections.body: 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F has to match on Polygonscan. Ethereum Tether, 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, uses chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, and Etherscan, and it has its own allowance rules. Those rules are not this token. If a receiver pasted the Ethereum address, this route is wrong. If they pasted Circle's native USDC on Polygon, this route is also wrong.

sections.heading: POL is the gas people still call by an old name
sections.body: The fee token on chain id 137 is POL. A wallet label that still says MATIC is a habit, not a second asset you can skip. USDT will not pay the transfer. The sentinel marks POL, not the Tether contract. Arrive with dollars and an empty POL line and you cannot move the dollars. Fund POL first, or buy it with a different route.

sections.heading: The wallet family changes at the bridge
sections.body: Phantom holds the Circle mint and cannot hold the Polygon ERC-20. MetaMask holds the ERC-20 only after you select chain id 137. Native SOL must remain for the source signature. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana to revoke. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the arrival. Solscan going quiet on your mint is the debit, not proof that Polygonscan has updated.

sections.heading: Keep the dollar on Solana when Polygon was never required
sections.body: Circle and Tether both have SPL mints. A local swap avoids POL, chain id 137, and a second wallet. Cross when the instruction names 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. The minimum USDT is the floor. This page will not turn a Polygon block into a delivery time. Wait on the destination address.

faqs.question: Does Solana USDC arrive as USDC on Polygon?
faqs.answer: No. Circle's mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v leaves Solana and Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F is what can arrive on Polygon, chain id 137. Circle's Polygon USDC is a different contract. Check Polygonscan. POL pays gas. If the receiver said Circle, this route is wrong. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

faqs.question: Will the USDT pay Polygon fees?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is POL, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on chain id 137. Hold POL before you move Tether. Phantom signed the SPL side and will not show this ERC-20. There is no ERC-20 approval on the Solana mint. Keep native SOL so that signature can be sent.

faqs.question: Is this the same USDT as on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan. This route credits Polygon only. Check Polygonscan. A mainnet allowance reset does not apply to the Polygon contract. Read the minimum before you sign. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

intro:
Swap USDC from Solana to WETH on Polygon. Circle's SPL mint leaves Solana, and Polygon WETH is what can arrive. The wrapper cannot pay POL gas.

Spend EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v in Phantom. Solscan is the source explorer, and there is no ERC-20 approval. WETH is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygon, chain id 137. Polygonscan is the check. Native gas is POL at 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1. Arbitrum and Base use other addresses. WBTC is not this token and is not native bitcoin.
description: Circle USDC leaves Solana and WETH arrives on Polygon. WETH cannot pay POL gas. Check Solscan and Polygonscan before you sign the quote. Read the minimum.

sections.heading: Polygon's WETH address is not mainnet's
sections.body: Pasting 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 into a Polygon token list does not create this balance. Etherscan and about 12 second blocks belong to chain id 1. This quote delivers 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 only, proved on Polygonscan, chain id 137. If the pool you must call is on Ethereum, you have bridged to the wrong wrapper. Bridging back costs a second hop.

sections.heading: POL remains the fee after WETH shows up
sections.body: A wallet full of WETH and empty of POL cannot deposit the WETH. If the error you are solving is insufficient gas, this page is the wrong route. Buy POL instead. If a contract names the WETH address, this arrival matches and the gas coin is still a separate problem. The sentinel is POL, not the wrapper, and not the Circle mint you spent.

sections.heading: Phantom signs, then an EVM wallet on 137 receives
sections.body: MetaMask cannot display the SPL mint leaving. Phantom cannot display Polygon WETH. Keep native SOL for the source fee. There is no allowance on Solana to clear. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is why the destination contract is new. Do not send the mint twice because Polygonscan has not caught up with Solscan.

sections.heading: A dollar on Polygon is a different request
sections.body: Circle's native USDC there is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Tether is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Bridged USDC.e is yet another contract. WETH is ether exposure. Use this page only when that exposure, at this address, is what you will hold. The minimum WETH is the floor. A local Solana swap is smaller when you did not need Polygon at all.

faqs.question: Can Polygon WETH from Solana USDC pay gas?
faqs.answer: No. WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 is an ERC-20. Gas on Polygon, chain id 137, is POL. Circle's mint left Solana. Hold POL before you move the wrapper. Check Polygonscan. If you only needed fees, this route is the wrong one. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

faqs.question: Is this the canonical WETH on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1, explorer Etherscan, blocks about 12 seconds. This route credits Polygon only. Arbitrum and Base use different WETH addresses too. If the pool is not on chain id 137, do not sell the Solana mint into this contract.

faqs.question: Does Phantom approve the USDC mint?
faqs.answer: No. EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v is an SPL mint with no ERC-20 approval. Solscan records the send. Keep native SOL for the fee. The WETH arrives in an EVM wallet on chain id 137, and that wallet still needs POL, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, to move it. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

intro:
Swap USDC from Solana to POL on Polygon. Circle's SPL mint leaves Solana, and native POL is what can arrive to pay gas on chain id 137.

You send EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Phantom signs, Solscan records it, and there is no ERC-20 approval. POL is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the native gas sentinel, on Polygon. Polygonscan shows the native balance, not a token import of the sentinel. This is not WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619, not Tether, and not ETH on Ethereum, chain id 1.
description: Circle USDC leaves Solana and native POL arrives on Polygon. POL pays gas on chain id 137. Check Solscan and Polygonscan before you sign the quote now.

sections.heading: POL is the fee coin, whatever the wallet still calls it
sections.body: Older interfaces say MATIC. The gas asset on chain id 137 is POL. This route buys that native balance. You do not approve the sentinel. If a screen asks you to import 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE as an ERC-20, close it and read the POL row after the network is Polygon. WETH will not pay the fee. USDC will not pay it either, on either chain.

sections.heading: Mainnet ETH is a different tank
sections.body: Ethereum, chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, Etherscan, charges ETH. Polygon charges POL. Filling one does not fill the other. If a dapp on Ethereum says you are out of gas, this POL will not help. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the network you are funding. A wallet left on Solana or on Ethereum will hide the arrival and tempt a second send.

sections.heading: SOL has to exist before POL can be requested
sections.body: Native SOL pays Phantom. The Circle mint does not. Keep a remainder or the hop never starts. MetaMask cannot show EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v leaving. There is no ERC-20 approval on that mint. Afterward, the EVM wallet on chain id 137 should show POL without an extra wrap. If you needed WETH for a pool, you bought the fee coin instead of the inventory.

sections.heading: Buy POL when Polygon transactions are the reason
sections.body: If you needed Tether or Circle on Polygon, a dollar route avoids POL's price. If you needed to stay on Solana, do not bridge. The minimum POL should cover more than a single failed attempt, because retries also burn POL. This page does not set a delivery time. Watch Polygonscan for the native balance on the destination address.

faqs.question: Is POL from this route the same as WETH?
faqs.answer: No. POL is native gas, quoted as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Polygon, chain id 137. WETH is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 and cannot pay fees. Circle's mint left Solana. Check the POL row on Polygonscan. If a contract wants WETH, this page is the wrong arrival. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Can this POL pay Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan, fee coin ETH. POL pays chain id 137 only. Phantom cannot hold POL, and an EVM wallet must be on Polygon to see it. SOL paid the source. There is no ERC-20 approval on the Solana USDC mint.

faqs.question: Why might the wallet still say MATIC?
faqs.answer: The gas token was renamed in many interfaces, and some wallets lag. The asset you receive is POL on chain id 137. Do not import the sentinel as a second token to force the old name. Confirm the native balance on Polygonscan. Keep SOL in Phantom so the Circle mint can leave.

intro:
Swap USDT from Solana to USDC on Polygon. Tether's SPL mint leaves Solana, and Circle's native USDC is what can arrive on Polygon. Bridged USDC.e is a different contract.

Send Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB from Phantom. Solscan is the explorer, and there is no ERC-20 approval. Circle on Polygon is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, chain id 137. Polygonscan is the check. Gas is POL at 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Ethereum's Circle USDC is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, Etherscan, and it is not this balance.
description: Tether USDT leaves Solana and Circle USDC arrives on Polygon. It is not bridged USDC.e. Pay SOL, then POL. Check Solscan and Polygonscan before you sign.

sections.heading: Native USDC will not fill an old USDC.e deposit
sections.body: Plenty of Polygon apps still point at bridged USDC.e. This route delivers 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. If the deposit box names the bridged contract, you will hold Circle dollars on chain id 137 and still be rejected. Check the address on Polygonscan before you treat the ticker as success. The fix is a different destination, not another signature on this quote.

sections.heading: Tether does not quietly become the fee coin
sections.body: You leave Tether's mint and arrive in Circle. Neither pays POL. The sentinel is the gas. A wallet with USDC and no POL cannot approve or transfer. Phantom cannot show the ERC-20, and MetaMask cannot show the mint. Keep SOL for the source. Switch the EVM wallet to 137 before you decide the credit failed.

sections.heading: Mainnet Circle is chain id 1
sections.body: Etherscan and about 12 second blocks describe that USDC, not this one. A payroll file that copied the Ethereum address will not match Polygonscan. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the arrival network. The bridge wait is separate from both explorers, and this page will not name it. Do not resend Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB because the EVM wallet is on the wrong chain.

sections.heading: Stay in Tether if the Polygon app said Tether
sections.body: Polygon USDT is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. If that is the contract in the invoice, this Circle arrival is the wrong page. If the dollars never needed to leave Solana, swap mints locally. The minimum USDC is the floor. Issuer plus bridge is a real cost even when both tickers say a dollar.

faqs.question: Does this route deliver bridged USDC.e on Polygon?
faqs.answer: No. Tether's mint leaves Solana and Circle's native USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 arrives on Polygon, chain id 137. USDC.e is a different contract. Check Polygonscan. If the app still names the bridged token, this page is the wrong arrival. POL is required to move the USDC.

faqs.question: What pays gas after the USDC lands?
faqs.answer: POL, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on chain id 137. USDC cannot. Hold POL in the EVM wallet. Phantom signed Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB with native SOL and will not display the Polygon token. There is no ERC-20 approval on that mint. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

faqs.question: Is this the Ethereum USDC contract?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Circle is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan. This credit is Polygon only. If the receiver pasted the mainnet address, do not use this route. Confirm 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

intro:
Swap USDT from Solana to WETH on Polygon. Tether's SPL mint leaves Solana, and Polygon WETH is what can arrive. You receive wrapped ether, not POL.

The mint is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Phantom and Solscan handle it with no ERC-20 approval. WETH is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on chain id 137. Polygonscan is the check. POL is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and is not included. Mainnet WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, Etherscan. WBTC is a different wrapper and is not native bitcoin.
description: Tether USDT leaves Solana and WETH arrives on Polygon. WETH is not the POL fee token. Check Solscan and Polygonscan before you sign the quote. Read it.

sections.heading: The wrapper and the fee are a pair of balances
sections.body: After this hop you can hold 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 and still fail the deposit, because chain id 137 bills POL. If gas was the shortage, buy POL and skip this page. If the contract names this WETH, you are in the right place and you still bring POL. Ethereum's WETH will not be accepted by that Polygon function. A copied mainnet address is a zero balance, not a shortcut.

sections.heading: Tether's mint does not approve itself on Solana
sections.body: There is no ERC-20 allowance in Phantom. Native SOL pays the signature. MetaMask stays blind until the asset is the Polygon ERC-20 and the network is 137. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the handoff. Solscan confirming a debit is not Polygonscan confirming a credit. Wait. A second send sells more Tether.

sections.heading: Other WETH contracts are other chains
sections.body: Arbitrum uses 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Base uses the predeploy 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. None of those balances update because Polygon did. If your liquidity is on those networks, this route is the wrong inventory. Etherscan's 12 second blocks describe mainnet, not this hop and not chain id 137.

sections.heading: A stablecoin route is quieter when you did not want ether
sections.body: USDT to USDC on Polygon keeps a dollar, with the warning that native USDC is not USDC.e. This page sells the dollar for WETH. Take it when you will hold the wrapper. The minimum WETH is the floor. POL still has to be in the wallet afterward, so a perfect WETH amount with zero POL is not a finished setup.

faqs.question: Does this WETH pay Polygon gas?
faqs.answer: No. 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 cannot pay fees. POL, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, pays them on chain id 137. Tether's mint left Solana. Check Polygonscan and hold POL before you move WETH. If fees were the only gap, this route is wrong. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

faqs.question: Is Polygon WETH the same as Ethereum WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum's contract is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1, Etherscan, about 12 second blocks. This route delivers the Polygon address only. Base and Arbitrum are different again. If the pool is not on chain id 137, do not bridge the Solana mint here. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

faqs.question: Is there an approval on the Solana USDT?
faqs.answer: No. Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB is an SPL mint. Phantom signs it, Solscan records it, and there is nothing to revoke. Keep native SOL for the fee. intro:

intro:

SOL is So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 in the quote, the wrapped mint. Phantom signs, Solscan shows it, native SOL pays the source fee, and there is no ERC-20 approval. ETH is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 42161, not Nova. Arbiscan shows the native row. This is not WETH, not mainnet ETH on chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, Etherscan, and not WBTC.
description: SOL leaves Solana and native ETH arrives on Arbitrum One. Both are gas coins on different networks. Check Solscan and Arbiscan before you sign the quote.

sections.heading: Wrapped SOL in, native ETH out, nothing imported
sections.body: Do not paste the mint into an EVM box and do not import the sentinel as a token. Read the ETH line on chain id 42161. If you sell every native SOL, Phantom cannot pay for the sale. The ETH you want cannot pay that Solana fee in advance. WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is the wrapper route if a contract refuses native ETH.

sections.heading: Mainnet and Nova are the two wrong maps
sections.body: A request for chain id 1 gas is a different bridge. A wallet on Nova will not show this ETH. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) is the only arrival. About 12 second blocks describe Ethereum, not this hop. WBTC is not delivered, and WBTC is not native bitcoin. If someone asked for bitcoin or for mainnet ether, stop.

sections.heading: Solscan empty is not Arbiscan full
sections.body: The debit can complete while the credit is still in the bridge. This page will not clock that gap. Do not sign a second time because Phantom dropped and MetaMask, on the wrong network, shows nothing. Switch to 42161 and watch the destination address. There is no ERC-20 approval on the mint to undo.

sections.heading: Buy this ETH only for Arbitrum transactions
sections.body: If you need SOL fees, selling SOL is backwards. If you need USDC or USDT, a dollar route is calmer. If you need ARB, you are buying a governance token, not gas. The minimum ETH should cover the L2 actions you already intend. Refuse a floor that leaves you short on the chain you just paid to enter.

faqs.question: Why are the SOL and ETH addresses different styles?
faqs.answer: SOL is the wrapped mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 on Solscan, held in Phantom, with no ERC-20 approval. ETH is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, shown on Arbiscan. Native SOL still pays the source fee. The balances cannot pay each other's chains. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Can this ETH pay Ethereum mainnet?
faqs.answer: No. Mainnet is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan. This ETH pays Arbitrum One, not Nova. If mainnet gas was the goal, this route is the wrong destination. Leave enough SOL in Phantom that the source transaction can still be signed. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

faqs.question: What if the contract wants WETH?
faqs.answer: Use the WETH route. Native ETH will not match 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 until you wrap, and wrapping needs ETH for gas. If the ABI names the wrapper, this page is incomplete. Check Arbiscan for whichever asset you chose to receive. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

intro:

Mainnet WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, Etherscan. WBTC is not this token and is not native bitcoin.
description: SOL leaves Solana and WETH arrives on Arbitrum One. The wrapper cannot pay gas. Keep SOL, then ETH. Check Solscan and Arbiscan before you sign the quote.

sections.heading: Only this WETH address counts on Arbitrum One
sections.body: Polygon, Base, and Ethereum use other contracts. A pool on those networks cannot see 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. If your liquidity is on chain id 1, this route is a detour. Etherscan will not show the credit. Arbiscan will, on 42161, not on Nova. Selling SOL into the wrong wrapper means a second bridge before you can deposit.

sections.heading: SOL out, ETH beside the wrapper
sections.body: Drain native SOL and the mint never leaves. Arrive with WETH and no ETH and the deposit never starts. This page does not buy the fee coin. Buy native ETH if gas is the error on the screen. Buy WETH if the ABI names the wrapper. The two fixes are not substitutes.

sections.heading: No Solana allowance, no shared timer
sections.body: There is nothing to revoke in Phantom. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the lock and the release. About 12 second blocks are Ethereum's, not a promise about Arbiscan. Wait for the WETH contract on the destination address. A second SOL signature doubles the sale while the first may still complete.

sections.heading: Dollars or ETH are the alternatives when WETH is not in the call
sections.body: Circle and Tether keep a dollar. Native ETH pays fees. ARB is governance. WETH is for a contract that asks for it. Read the minimum. If the ether you would hold is less than you will give up in SOL, do not sign. A local swap on Solana never needs chain id 42161.

faqs.question: Can WETH from SOL pay Arbitrum gas?
faqs.answer: No. 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is an ERC-20. ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, pays chain id 42161, not Nova. SOL left as the wrapped mint. Hold ETH and check Arbiscan. If you needed fees only, this route is wrong. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

faqs.question: Is this the canonical WETH on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. That address is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1, Etherscan, about 12 second blocks. This route credits Arbitrum One only. If the pool is not on 42161, the wrapper you receive is inventory that pool cannot spend. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

faqs.question: Can I spend all my SOL to buy ARB?

Snowtrace is the proof. Selling SOL into the wrong dollar is painful to unwind. If the app said Tether, the contract is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 and this page is the wrong route.

sections.heading: Leave native SOL or the mint stays
sections.body: So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 names the asset. Native SOL pays. There is no ERC-20 approval. MetaMask cannot confirm the debit. After the hop, USDC cannot pay chain id 43114. Bring AVAX or the dollars sit still. An X-Chain wallet will not show them and cannot spend them.

sections.heading: C-Chain is the only Avalanche view that counts
sections.body: [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the switch from Phantom to an EVM wallet on 43114. The bridge has no clock here. Do not send SOL twice because an X-Chain screen is empty. Wait for the Circle contract on the destination address in Snowtrace.

sections.heading: A Solana mint is enough when you are not leaving
sections.body: Circle's SPL mint is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. A local swap never asks for AVAX or risks USDC.e. Cross when someone named the C-Chain contract. The minimum USDC is the floor. A thin conversion of SOL into a dollar should be refused even though the output is a stablecoin. USDC.e will not match this Circle contract, and X-Chain will not show the balance.

faqs.question: Is USDC from SOL the bridged USDC.e on Avalanche?
faqs.answer: No. Circle at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E arrives on C-Chain, chain id 43114. USDC.e is different. SOL left as the wrapped mint. Check Snowtrace. If the app wants the bridged token, this route is wrong. AVAX is required to move the USDC. X-Chain will not show it. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

faqs.question: Can I sell all of my SOL?
faqs.answer: No. Native SOL pays Phantom. The quote says So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 and has no ERC-20 approval. Leave a remainder. On C-Chain, hold AVAX, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, or the new USDC cannot transfer on chain id 43114. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.

faqs.question: What if the receiver wants Tether?
faqs.answer: This page is wrong. Tether is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Circle will not satisfy that address. Switch routes before you sell SOL. Confirm the contract on Snowtrace, and do not look for an ERC-20 on the X-Chain. Do not send a second time while the first transfer is still open.

intro:
Swap SOL from Solana to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. SOL leaves Solana, and Tether on C-Chain is what can arrive. AVAX pays the fee after that. X-Chain will not show the token.

The mint in the quote is So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. Phantom signs, Solscan shows it, native SOL pays, and there is no ERC-20 approval. Tether is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on chain id 43114. Snowtrace is the check. The gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is AVAX. Circle is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E if you needed Circle instead. Ethereum's Tether is a different chain.
description: SOL leaves Solana and Tether USDT arrives on Avalanche C-Chain. AVAX pays the next fee. Keep SOL for the source. Check Solscan and Snowtrace. Read the minimum.

sections.heading: C-Chain Tether is not Circle and not Ethereum USDT
sections.body: 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 is the arrival. Circle will not satisfy a Tether invoice, and this Tether will not satisfy a Circle invoice. Ethereum's USDT, with its allowance reset, lives on chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, Etherscan. Do not import that address on Avalanche. Snowtrace has to show the C-Chain contract. USDC.e is yet another miss.

sections.heading: The SOL fee is paid before Snowtrace matters
sections.body: Drain native SOL and the wrapped mint never leaves. There is no ERC-20 approval in Phantom. MetaMask cannot watch So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. After the hop, USDT cannot pay chain id 43114. An EVM wallet with no AVAX is stuck, and an X-Chain wallet will not even display the token.

sections.heading: Look at chain id 43114, then wait
sections.body: [Avalanche C-Chain](/chains/avalanche) is the destination. The bridge does not publish a finish time. Do not treat an empty X-Chain screen as a failure, and do not send a second SOL transfer because of it. Wait for the Tether contract on the destination address. Both sends can complete if you are impatient.

sections.heading: A local Tether mint is the smaller trade
sections.body: Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB is Tether on Solana. Use it when the dollar can stay an SPL token. Cross when the C-Chain address is required. The minimum USDT is the floor. Selling SOL into a stablecoin is only sensible if that floor preserves what you needed.

faqs.question: Does SOL become Circle USDC on Avalanche?
faqs.answer: No. Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 is the arrival on C-Chain, chain id 43114. Circle is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. SOL left as the wrapped mint. Check Snowtrace. If the receiver said Circle, this route is wrong. AVAX is required to move the USDT. X-Chain will not show it. Confirm the contract on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Why keep SOL while selling SOL?
faqs.answer: Native SOL pays the Phantom fee. The quote's mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 does not remove that need, and there is no ERC-20 approval. Leave a remainder. On C-Chain, hold AVAX, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, or the USDT cannot move on chain id 43114. Keep the destination gas token or the arrival cannot move.

faqs.question: Is this Ethereum's USDT?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether is on chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan, and it has its own allowance behavior. This route credits C-Chain only. Confirm 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Snowtrace before you sell SOL. Do not look for it on the X-Chain. The quote minimum is the floor, and a thin floor is a reason to stop.

intro:
Swap SOL from Solana to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. SOL leaves Solana, and native AVAX is what can arrive. You trade one fee coin for C-Chain gas, not for an X-Chain balance.

SOL is So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 in the quote, the wrapped mint. Phantom signs, Solscan shows it, native SOL pays the source fee, and there is no ERC-20 approval. AVAX is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 43114. Snowtrace shows the native row. This is not Circle, not Tether, and not ETH on Ethereum, chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, Etherscan. WBTC is not an output and is not native bitcoin.
description: SOL leaves Solana and native AVAX arrives on Avalanche C-Chain. Both are gas coins on different chains. Check Solscan and Snowtrace before you sign now.

sections.heading: Two gas coins, and only C-Chain AVAX arrives
sections.body: Do not paste the wrapped SOL mint into an EVM field, and do not paste the sentinel into Phantom. Read the AVAX line on chain id 43114. X-Chain and P-Chain are the wrong Avalanche chains. If you empty native SOL, Phantom cannot pay for the sale. The AVAX you want cannot pay that Solana fee. USDC and USDT routes exist if you needed a dollar instead of gas.

sections.heading: Mainnet ETH is a different request
sections.body: Chain id 1 uses Etherscan and about 12 second blocks. This AVAX will not pay it. [Avalanche C-Chain](/chains/avalanche) is the only network this credit spends. If someone asked for Ethereum gas, for WETH, or for bitcoin via WBTC, this page does not answer them. WBTC is not native bitcoin, and it is not what SOL is becoming here.

sections.heading: An empty X-Chain screen is not a missing bridge
sections.body: Snowtrace on 43114 is the credit. Solscan is the debit. The gap between them is the bridge, and this page will not clock it. Do not send a second SOL transfer because the wrong Avalanche chain looks empty. There is no ERC-20 approval on the mint to reverse a duplicate.

sections.heading: Cross only when you will transact on C-Chain
sections.body: If you need SOL for Solana fees, selling it is backwards. If you need a dollar, Circle or Tether is the calmer arrival. The minimum AVAX should cover the C-Chain actions you already intend, including a retry. Refuse a floor that leaves the new chain unable to broadcast.

faqs.question: Are the SOL mint and the AVAX sentinel the same kind of address?
faqs.answer: No. SOL is So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 on Solscan, held in Phantom, with no ERC-20 approval. AVAX is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on C-Chain, chain id 43114, shown on Snowtrace. Native SOL still pays the source fee. X-Chain AVAX is not this credit, and neither coin pays the other network. A block interval is not a delivery time for the bridge.

faqs.question: Can this AVAX pay Ethereum fees?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum is chain id 1, about 12 second blocks, explorer Etherscan, fee coin ETH. This AVAX pays C-Chain only. If mainnet gas was the goal, this route is the wrong destination. Leave enough SOL in Phantom that the source transaction can still be signed.

faqs.question: What if I needed USDC or USDT instead of AVAX?
faqs.answer: Use the matching dollar route. Circle is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E and Tether is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Native AVAX will not satisfy either contract. This page is for C-Chain gas. Check Snowtrace on chain id 43114, not the X-Chain. Switch the wallet to the destination chain before you judge the balance.
